mbpp_0189.reference_description: Write a java function to find the first missing positive number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the first missing positive number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: In-place First Missing Positive

Main goal: Given an int array, compute the smallest positive integer not present in the array using O(n) time and O(1) extra space by performing in-place marking.

What the code does:
- It scans for the presence of 1. If 1 is missing, it immediately returns 1.
- It normalizes the array by replacing non-positive numbers and numbers greater than n with 1.
- It marks the presence of values 1..n by, for each element, using (value-1) as an index and adding n to that position in order to flag it.
- After marking, it scans the array to find the first index i where the value at i is <= n, which means i+1 is missing; it returns i+1.
- If all 1..n are present, it returns n+1.

Notes: The code is obfuscated/ Decompiled, using helper methods with single-letter names that correspond to basic comparisons (equality and ordering). The overall approach matches the classic in-place solution for the “First Missing Positive” problem.

mbpp_0159.reference_description: Write a function to print the season for the given month and day.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to print the season for the given month and day.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
- Title: SeasonFinder.monthSeason
- Main goal: Given a month name and a day, determine the season (winter, spring, summer, autumn).
- How it works: 
  - It first assigns a season based on the month alone (Jan/Feb/Mar → winter; Apr/May/Jun → spring; Jul/Aug/Sep → summer; Oct/Nov/Dec → autumn).
  - It then refines this result using day thresholds to align with common season boundaries: March > 19 (Mar 20+) → spring; June > 20 (Jun 21+) → summer; September > 21 (Sep 22+) → autumn; December > 20 (Dec 21+) → winter.
- Notes: The code uses obfuscated helper methods (I, l, Il) to implement boolean checks and contains several no-op lines typical of decompiled code.

mbpp_0771.reference_description: Write a function to check if the given expression is balanced or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if the given expression is balanced or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: ExpressionChecker - Balanced Bracket Validator
Main goal: Determine whether a string contains properly nested and matched pairs of parentheses (), braces {}, and brackets [], using a stack. Non-bracket characters are ignored. The function returns true only if all opening brackets are closed in the correct order and the string length is even; otherwise, it returns false.

mbpp_0323.reference_description: Write a function to re-arrange the given array in alternating positive and negative items.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to re-arrange the given array in alternating positive and negative items.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Right-rotation based in-place rearrangement to enforce alternating sign

Main goal: The code reorders an int array in place by using a right-rotation of a subarray (moving the element at index n2 to n, shifting the middle right by one) to progressively place elements so that even indices hold non-negative numbers and odd indices hold negative numbers, effectively achieving an alternating-sign arrangement through a stateful scan and conditional rotations.

mbpp_0522.reference_description: Write a function to find the longest bitonic subsequence for the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the longest bitonic subsequence for the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Longest Bitonic Subsequence Length
Main goal: Given an integer array, compute the length of the Longest Bitonic Subsequence (increasing then decreasing) by calculating, for each index, the length of the Longest Increasing Subsequence ending at that index and the Longest Decreasing Subsequence starting at that index, then taking the maximum of their sum minus 1.

mbpp_0039.reference_description: Write a function to check if the letters of a given string can be rearranged so that two characters that are adjacent to each other are different.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if the letters of a given string can be rearranged so that two characters that are adjacent to each other are different.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Reorganizes an input string so that no two adjacent characters are the same by counting character frequencies and repeatedly selecting the two most frequent characters (via a priority queue) to build the result; if impossible (a character occurs more than (n+1)/2 times), returns an empty string; uses an inner Node to store a character and its remaining count.

mbpp_0245.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum sum of bi-tonic sub-sequence for the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum sum of bi-tonic sub-sequence for the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Maximum Sum Increasing Subsequence (MSIS) DP
Main goal: Compute the maximum possible sum of a strictly increasing subsequence in the input array by using two DP passes (one for the best sum ending at each index and one for the best sum starting at each index) and then combining them to obtain the overall maximum.

mbpp_0776.reference_description: Write a function to count those characters which have vowels as their neighbors in the given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to count those characters which have vowels as their neighbors in the given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Analysis of Solution.countVowels

Main goal: The function counts how many consonants in the input string are adjacent to vowels (from the set "aeiou"). It iterates through interior positions to count consonants with at least one neighboring vowel and also checks the first and last characters for adjacency to a vowel. The result is the total number of such consonants, not the number of vowels.

mbpp_0223.reference_description: Write a function to check for majority element in the given sorted array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check for majority element in the given sorted array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Goal: Determine if a given value occurs more than n/2 times (i.e., is a majority) in the first n elements of an array.

What it does: It finds the leftmost index of the target value using a binary search, then checks whether the element at leftmostIndex + floor(n/2) exists and equals the target. If so, the value is a majority; otherwise not. Assumes the array is sorted so duplicates of the same value are consecutive.

Key functions:
- isMajority(nArray, n, n2): orchestrates the check and returns true if n2 is a majority.
- binarySearch(nArray, low, high, target): returns the index of the first occurrence of target in [low, high], or -1 if not found.
- Helper boolean methods (I, Il, l, IIl, ll) are tiny inlined comparisons used by the decompiled code.

mbpp_0515.reference_description: Write a function to check if there is a subset with sum divisible by m.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if there is a subset with sum divisible by m.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Subset Sum Modulo Checker
Main goal: To determine whether there exists a non-empty subset of the given integers whose sum is divisible by n2.
Approach (brief): Uses a boolean array of size n2 to track which residues modulo n2 are reachable. For each input number, it updates the reachable residues by adding the number to previously reachable sums (mod n2) and also includes the number itself. If residue 0 becomes reachable, it returns true; otherwise, after processing all elements, it returns whether residue 0 is reachable. It also short-circuits with a known fact: if the count of numbers n > modulus n2, a subset with sum divisible by n2 exists (pigeonhole principle).

mbpp_0069.reference_description: Write a function to check whether array contains the given sublist or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check whether array contains the given sublist or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: SublistChecker - detects if one list is a contiguous sublist of another.

Main goal: To determine whether list2 appears as a contiguous sublist within list. The static method isSublist handles edge cases (empty list2, exact equality, and when list2 is larger than list) and then performs a linear scan over possible start indices in list, checking element-by-element for a full match. If a match is found, it returns true; otherwise, it returns false. The code uses small, obfuscated helper methods for basic comparisons (<=, <, >, !=) but the core logic is a simple sublist search.

mbpp_0123.reference_description: Write a function to sum all amicable numbers from 1 to a specified number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to sum all amicable numbers from 1 to a specified number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: AmicableNumbers - Sum of amicable numbers up to n
Main goal: Given a positive integer n, the code identifies amicable number pairs (a, b) where sumOfDivisors(a) = b, sumOfDivisors(b) = a, and a ≠ b, by scanning integers a from 2 to n. If such a pair is found, both a and b are stored in a set to avoid double counting. After the scan, the code returns the sum of all stored numbers (the sum of all amicable numbers associated with a ≤ n, including their partners even if the partner > n). The helper methods implement the sum of proper divisors and simple boolean checks; the extra seemingly useless statements are artifacts from decompilation.

mbpp_0408.reference_description: Write a function to find k number of pairs which consist of one element from the first array and one element from the second array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find k number of pairs which consist of one element from the first array and one element from the second array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: K Smallest Pairs by Sum using a Min-Heap
Main goal: Given two int arrays and an integer k, produce up to k pairs [a[i], b[j]] with the smallest sums a[i] + b[j], using a PriorityQueue (min-heap) to explore the matrix of possible sums starting from (0,0) and expanding to (i+1,j) and (i,j+1). The code includes input validation (non-empty arrays and k > 0). It returns the list of pairs in ascending order of their sums.

mbpp_0747.reference_description: Write a function to find the longest common subsequence for the given three string sequence.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the longest common subsequence for the given three string sequence.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Three-String Longest Common Subsequence Length (LCS3)
Main goal: Compute the length of the longest common subsequence among three input strings using a 3D dynamic programming table. The DP state dp[i][j][k] stores the LCS length for prefixes of lengths i, j, and k. If the last characters of all three strings match, it uses dp[i-1][j-1][k-1] + 1; otherwise it takes the maximum of dp[i-1][j][k], dp[i][j-1][k], and dp[i][j][k-1]. Returns dp[n][n2][n3]. The code includes small helper functions for basic condition checks and is presented in an obfuscated/decompiled style.

mbpp_0838.reference_description: Write a java function to find minimum number swaps required to make two binary strings equal.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find minimum number swaps required to make two binary strings equal.

mbpp_0423.reference_description: Write a function to solve gold mine problem.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to solve gold mine problem.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The GoldMine class implements a dynamic programming solution to the Gold Mine problem. getMaxGold(int[][] grid, int n, int n2) computes the maximum amount of gold that can be collected by moving from left to right across a grid (n rows, n2 columns) where from each cell you may move to the cell to the right, diagonally up-right, or diagonally down-right. It builds a DP table by processing columns from right to left: dp[r][c] = grid[r][c] + max(dp[r][c+1], dp[r-1][c+1], dp[r+1][c+1]) with appropriate boundary checks, then returns the maximum value found in the leftmost column. The helper methods are simple boundary/comparison checks used during the DP transitions. The code appears obfuscated/decompiled.

mbpp_0940.reference_description: Write a function to sort the given array by using heap sort.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to sort the given array by using heap sort.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: It implements heap sort for an int array. It first builds a max-heap with heapify, then repeatedly swaps the root (maximum) with the last element and shifts down the new root to restore the heap, shrinking the heap size each iteration to produce an in-place ascending sort. The code uses several small boolean helpers for index/bound checks and contains decompiler artifacts with obfuscated variable names.

mbpp_0387.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the hexadecimal number is even or odd.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the hexadecimal number is even or odd.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: EvenOrOddHex - Check parity of the last hex digit
Main goal: Return "Even" if the last character of the input string represents an even hexadecimal digit; otherwise return "Odd".
How it works: It takes the last character and effectively checks if it is one of the hex digits {0, 2, 4, 6, 8, A, C, E}. If so, it returns "Even"; otherwise it returns "Odd". The code uses two helper methods with obfuscated names to perform simple equality/inequality checks.

mbpp_0628.reference_description: Write a function to replace all spaces in the given string with character * array item * array item * array item * array item '%20'.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to replace all spaces in the given string with character * array item * array item * array item * array item '%20'.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code implements a URL-encoding-for-spaces transformation. It trims the input, counts spaces to compute the required new length, returns "-1" if the result would exceed 1000 characters, then builds a new string by replacing each space with the three-character sequence "%20" (processing from the end to shift characters as needed), and finally returns the transformed string.

mbpp_0315.reference_description: Write a java function to find the first maximum length of even word.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the first maximum length of even word.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Longest even-length word extractor
Main goal: From an input string containing spaces, return the longest word whose length is even. If no such word exists, return "-1". The method scans characters, counts lengths of tokens between spaces, updates the best starting index and length when an even-length token longer than the current best is found, and finally returns that substring.

mbpp_0901.reference_description: Write a function to find the smallest multiple of the first n numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the smallest multiple of the first n numbers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The class SmallestMultiple contains a method smallestMultiple(int n) that (a) handles n <= 2 by returning n, (b) builds a list of divisors in the upper half of the range (from floor(n/2)+1 up to n), and (c) starts with a candidate l = 2n and repeatedly increases l by n until l is divisible by every number in that upper-half list; when that condition holds, it returns l. The rest of the code consists of many obfuscated helper methods for simple comparisons (lIl, ll, l, Il, IIl) and a small comparator (I), plus several decompiler artifacts (no-op string-length branches) that do not affect the core logic. Overall, it’s a convoluted, inefficient, and not-robust attempt to compute the least common multiple of 1..n by checking divisibility against the top-half divisors only.

mbpp_0834.reference_description: Write a function to generate a square matrix filled with elements from 1 to n raised to the power of 2 in spiral order.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to generate a square matrix filled with elements from 1 to n raised to the power of 2 in spiral order.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Spiral Matrix Generator

Main goal: Generate an n-by-n matrix filled with the integers 1 to n^2 in clockwise spiral order, starting at the top-left corner. If n <= 0, return an empty matrix. The code uses four evolving boundaries (top, bottom, left, right) and fills the matrix layer by layer while incrementing the value.

mbpp_0516.reference_description: Write a function to sort array of elements using radix sort.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to sort array of elements using radix sort.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: LSD Radix Sort for int[]
Main goal: Sort an array of integers in ascending order using a base-10 least-significant-digit radix sort. The code determines the maximum value, then iteratively distributes elements into 10 buckets based on the current digit (n / n2 % 10) and concatenates the buckets back into the array, increasing the digit place (n2) by a factor of 10 each pass until all digits are processed. It uses ArrayList buckets and preserves stability across passes.

mbpp_0152.reference_description: Write a function to sort the given array by using merge sort.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to sort the given array by using merge sort.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MergeSort - Top-down Merge Sort for int Arrays

Main goal: Sort integers using the merge sort algorithm. The merge method combines two sorted int arrays into a single sorted array, and the mergeSort method recursively splits the input into halves, sorts each half, and merges them. Helper methods I, Il, and l perform simple comparisons and a null-check; the extra string-invocation lines are artifacts of decompilation and do not affect logic.

mbpp_0898.reference_description: Write a function to extract specified number of elements from a given array, which follow each other continuously.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to extract specified number of elements from a given array, which follow each other continuously.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Extractor of runs with exact length n

Main goal: Given a non-null, non-empty list of integers and a positive integer n, return a new list containing the values that form runs of exactly n consecutive identical numbers in the input list. It scans the list, counts consecutive equal elements, and when a run ends (or at the end of the list) it adds the value to the result if the run length equals n. If inputs are invalid (null, empty, or n <= 0), it returns an empty list.

mbpp_0665.reference_description: Write a java function to shift first element to the end of given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to shift first element to the end of given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Move all occurrences of the first element to the end in a new list

Main goal: Given a List<Integer>, return a new list where all elements not equal to the first element of the input appear first (preserving their original order), followed by all occurrences of the first element. If the input list is null or empty, return an empty list. The original list is not modified.

mbpp_0501.reference_description: Write a java function to find common divisor between two numbers in a given pair.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find common divisor between two numbers in a given pair.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: CommonDivisors - GCD computation and common-divisors counting (obfuscated)

Main goal: Provide methods to compute the greatest common divisor of two integers (ngcd) and to derive a count related to their common divisors (numCommDiv) by factoring the gcd. ngcd scans from 1 up to min(n, n2) to find the largest common divisor. numCommDiv computes the gcd first, then counts divisors up to sqrt(gcd), effectively returning a value close to half the total number of divisors of the gcd (ceil(d(gcd)/2)) due to an obfuscated counting approach. The code also contains intentionally obfuscated or dead-code lines.

mbpp_0938.reference_description: Write a function to find three closest elements from three sorted arrays.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find three closest elements from three sorted arrays.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Summary_description
Title: ClosestElements.findClosest - Minimal-range triple across three arrays
Main goal: Given three sorted int arrays and corresponding bounds n, n2, n3, find one element from each array (within those bounds) such that the difference between the maximum and minimum among the chosen trio is minimized. The method uses a three-pointer sweep: at each step it takes the current elements from each array, computes the min and max, updates the best triple if the range is smaller, and advances the pointer(s) that hold the current minimum value (one at a time). It returns the actual triple values (not indices). If a zero range is found, it exits early.

mbpp_0548.reference_description: Write a function to find the length of the longest increasing subsequence of the given sequence.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the length of the longest increasing subsequence of the given sequence.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Longest Increasing Subsequence Length Calculator (Dynamic Programming)

Main goal: Given an array of integers, compute the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence (LIS) using a classic O(n^2) dynamic programming approach. The code initializes a dp array to 1 for all positions, then for each pair (i, j) with j < i updates dp[i] = max(dp[i], dp[j] + 1) when a[i] > a[j]. Finally, it returns the maximum value in dp as the LIS length. Helper methods I and l control loop boundaries (n < m) and comparison (n > m) used in the logic.

mbpp_0149.reference_description: Write a function to find the longest subsequence such that the difference between adjacents is one for the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the longest subsequence such that the difference between adjacents is one for the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Longest subsequence with adjacent difference of 1
Main goal: Given an array and its length, compute the length of the longest subsequence (not necessarily contiguous) where consecutive elements differ by exactly 1 (absolute difference). It uses dynamic programming: dp[i] stores the best length ending at i, updating from all previous j where a[i] == a[j] ± 1. The result is the maximum value in dp.

mbpp_0060.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum length of the subsequence with difference between adjacent elements for the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum length of the subsequence with difference between adjacent elements for the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MaxSubsequence
Main goal: Compute the length of the longest non-contiguous subsequence of the input array where the absolute difference between consecutive elements is at most 1, using a dynamic programming approach. It initializes a dp array to 1 for each position, updates dp[i] = max(dp[i], dp[j] + 1) for all j < i with |a[i] - a[j]| <= 1, and returns the maximum dp value.

mbpp_0822.reference_description: Write a function to return true if the password is valid.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to return true if the password is valid.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: PasswordValidator - Multi-constraint password policy checker
Main goal: Implement passValidity(string) to return true only when the string length is between 6 and 12, contains at least one lowercase letter, one uppercase letter, one digit, and at least one of the characters $, #, or @, and contains no whitespace.

mbpp_0523.reference_description: Write a function to check whether a given string has a capital letter, a lower case letter, a number and specified length using lambda function.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check whether a given string has a capital letter, a lower case letter, a number and specified length using lambda function.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Goal: A Java string validator that checks four criteria and returns a list of messages describing any violations, or a single "Valid string." message if all checks pass.

What it does:
- Checks (via four lambdas) that the input has at least:
  - one uppercase letter
  - one lowercase letter
  - one digit
  - a minimum length (intended as 8, though the code uses a 7-based comparison)
- Applies all checks to the input and collects any failure messages; successful checks yield Boolean.TRUE and are filtered out.
- If there are no failure messages, adds "Valid string." to the result.
- Returns a List<String> containing either all failure messages or a single "Valid string." entry.

Helpers Il/I/l are tiny comparison utilities used by the checks.

mbpp_0550.reference_description: Write a java function to find the maximum element in a sorted and rotated array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the maximum element in a sorted and rotated array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Peak-finding in a bitonic array using binary search
Main goal: The findMax function searches for the maximum (peak) element in an array that increases up to a single peak and then decreases. It uses a binary-search-style approach over a given index range, with base cases for empty/singleton ranges and conditional checks on mid against its neighbors to decide which half to search next, ultimately returning the peak value.

mbpp_0468.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum product formed by multiplying numbers of an increasing subsequence of that array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum product formed by multiplying numbers of an increasing subsequence of that array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MaxProductIncreasingSubsequence
Main goal: Compute the maximum product obtainable from a strictly increasing subsequence of the input array. It uses dynamic programming: dp[i] stores the maximum product of an increasing subsequence that ends at index i (initialized to the element itself). For every pair i > j, if a[i] > a[j] and dp[i] < dp[j] * a[i], it updates dp[i] to dp[j] * a[i]. After processing, the result is the maximum value in dp[]. The code effectively finds the largest product among all increasing subsequences (in order) of the array.

mbpp_0524.reference_description: Write a function to find the sum of maximum increasing subsequence of the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the sum of maximum increasing subsequence of the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Title: Maximum Sum Increasing Subsequence (MSIS) Calculator. Main goal: Given an array, compute the maximum possible sum of any strictly increasing subsequence. It uses dynamic programming: for each index i, it builds dp[i] as the best sum of an increasing subsequence ending at i (initially a[i], then updated from previous j where a[i] > a[j]). The result is the maximum value in dp. Time complexity: O(n^2); Space: O(n).

mbpp_0755.reference_description: Write a function to find the second smallest number in array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the second smallest number in array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: SecondSmallestFinder – computes the second smallest distinct integer in a list.

Main goal: Return the second smallest unique value from a list of integers, or null if the input is invalid or there aren’t at least two distinct values.

What it does:
- Validates input is non-null and has at least two elements; returns null otherwise.
- If exactly two elements and they are equal, returns null (no second distinct value).
- Iterates the list to collect unique values (using a HashSet to track seen numbers) into an ArrayList.
- Sorts the list of unique values and returns the element at index 1 (the second smallest) if there are at least two unique values; otherwise returns null.

Notes:
- The code uses several tiny helper methods with trivial comparisons.
- The obfuscated-looking lines (e.g., empty string length checks) are no-ops inserted by decompilation and do not affect logic.

mbpp_0926.reference_description: Write a function to find n-th rencontres number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find n-th rencontres number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Rencontres Numbers and Binomial Coefficient Calculator
Main goal: Implement recursive computation of binomial coefficients C(n, k) and the rencontres numbers r(n, k) (permutations of n items with exactly k fixed points). It uses r(n, k) = C(n, k) * D(n − k), where D(m) (derangements) follows D(0)=1, D(1)=0, and D(m) = (m−1)(D(m−1) + D(m−2)). The code includes base-case handling for zero and equal parameters to drive these recurrences.

mbpp_0881.reference_description: Write a function to find the sum of first even and odd number of a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the sum of first even and odd number of a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: First Even + First Odd Sum

Main goal: Iterate a list of integers, capture the first even number and the first odd number (using -1 as a sentinel for "not found"), and return their sum when both exist. If one type is missing, return the partial sum (which may equal -1 or -2 if none are found).

What it does:
- Scans the list and stores the first even value in n and the first odd value in n2.
- Stops early once both have been found and returns n + n2.
- If only one (or neither) is found, returns the sum including the sentinel (-1) for any missing value.

Helper methods:
- l(int a, int b): checks a == b.
- I(int a): checks a != 0.
- Il(int a): checks a == 0.
- ll(int a, int b): checks a != b.

Overall, the code computes the sum of the first even and the first odd integers from the input list, with sentinel handling for missing parity values.

mbpp_0068.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the given array is monotonic or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the given array is monotonic or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Monotonicity Tester for Integer Arrays
Main goal: Determine if an int array is monotonic (non-decreasing or non-increasing); returns true for null or length < 2; otherwise returns false if the array has both increases and decreases.

mbpp_0850.reference_description: Write a function to check if a triangle of positive area is possible with the given angles.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if a triangle of positive area is possible with the given angles.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: TriangleUtils: Validates angle-like triples
Main goal: Check whether three integers can form a triangle by ensuring none are zero and their sum is 180. The auxiliary methods只是 wrappers around basic comparisons, and due to the sum==180 constraint, the inner conditions are effectively redundant.

mbpp_0455.reference_description: Write a function to check whether the given month number contains 31 days or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check whether the given month number contains 31 days or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MonthUtils.checkMonthNumber – membership test for specific months
Main goal: Determine if an input n represents one of the months {1, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12}. The function returns true when n equals any of these values and false otherwise. It uses helper methods I(n, m) for “n != m” and l(n, m) for “n == m”; due to negation, !I(n, m) equals (n == m), making the overall check effectively a set membership test.

mbpp_0866.reference_description: Write a function to check whether the given month name contains 31 days or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check whether the given month name contains 31 days or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Goal: Provide a MonthUtil.checkMonthNumb(String) method that checks whether the input string is one of a fixed set of month names (January, March, May, July, August, October, December) and returns true if it matches, false otherwise. It uses a hashCode-based switch to map those names to indices and then returns true for any valid index; otherwise false. The extra decompiler-like conditions and the I helper are artifacts of decompilation and do not affect the result.

mbpp_0907.reference_description: Write a function to print the first n lucky numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to print the first n lucky numbers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: LuckyNumbers — Sieve-based generator of the first n lucky numbers

Main goal: Generate the first n lucky numbers by starting with a list of odd numbers (and a leading -1 placeholder), then repeatedly filtering the list using a sieve where the current element determines which indices to keep, and finally return the first n numbers (excluding the initial -1). The program’s main method reads n from the command line and prints these numbers.

mbpp_0453.reference_description: Write a java function to find the sum of even factors of a number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the sum of even factors of a number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Even-numbered sigma(n) calculator (sum of divisors)

Main goal: Compute the sum of all positive divisors of n (the sigma function) for even inputs, returning 0 for odd inputs. It factors n via trial division up to sqrt(n); for each prime factor p^a it multiplies the running product by (1 + p + p^2 + ... + p^a). If a remaining factor remains after the loop (n ≥ 2), it multiplies by (1 + remaining). The helper methods are tiny, obfuscated wrappers around simple comparisons used to confuse the decompiled code.

mbpp_0074.reference_description: Write a function to check whether it follows the sequence given in the patterns array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check whether it follows the sequence given in the patterns array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: PatternChecker - Bijective Pattern Matching

Main goal: To determine if two string arrays of equal length form a bijective mapping between the pattern tokens (from the second array) and the words (from the first array), ensuring that each unique pattern maps to exactly one unique word and that the mapping is consistent across all positions.

mbpp_0031.reference_description: Write a function to find the top k integers that occur most frequently from given arrays of sorted and distinct integers using heap queue algorithm.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the top k integers that occur most frequently from given arrays of sorted and distinct integers using heap queue algorithm.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Top-N Frequent Integers Across Sub-Lists
Main goal: Given a List<List<Integer>> and an integer n, return a List<Integer> containing the n most frequent integers that appear across all sub-lists. The code builds a frequency map for all numbers, uses a min-heap (priority queue) to maintain the current top-n by frequency, and then collects the keys from the heap into the result list (in ascending frequency order). If there are fewer than n distinct integers, it returns all of them. Note: some odd, dead branches are artifacts of decompilation and do not affect the core logic.

mbpp_0463.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum product subarray of the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum product subarray of the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Implements maxSubarrayProduct: scans an int[] and computes the maximum product of any contiguous subarray. It maintains two running values per position—n2 (best positive product ending here) and n3 (best negative product ending here)—and updates a global maximum n4 when a larger product is found. The loop resets on zeros. After the pass, it returns the maximum product found (or 0 if no positive product was observed). The code uses small helper predicates (I, Il, l) and contains decompiler/debug noise; edge cases like all-negative inputs may not be handled in the standard way.

mbpp_0129.reference_description: Write a function to calculate magic square.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to calculate magic square.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MagicSquare - Row/Column/Diagonal Sum Equality Checker
Main goal: Determine whether a given 2D int array behaves like a magic square by computing the sums of all rows, all columns, and the main diagonal, then verifying that all these sums are equal (i.e., the set of sums has at most one distinct value).

mbpp_0113.reference_description: Write a function to check if a string represents an integer or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if a string represents an integer or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: IntegerChecker.checkInteger - Integer literal validator
Main goal: Determine whether a given string represents a valid integer literal (optional leading '+' or '-') consisting solely of digits. It returns:
- true if the string is a valid integer,
- false if it contains non-digit characters (or only a sign without digits),
- null if the input is empty after trimming.

mbpp_0854.reference_description: Write a function which accepts an arbitrary array and converts it to a heap using heap queue algorithm.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function which accepts an arbitrary array and converts it to a heap using heap queue algorithm.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: HeapUtil - Generic in-place heap construction for lists
Main goal: Convert a List<T> (where T implements Comparable) into a max-heap in place. The rawHeap method builds the heap by performing sift-down from the last non-leaf node up to the root, and the private siftDown method implements the percolate-down operation to restore the heap property at each step. The code uses small helper methods for simple index/size comparisons. Overall, it is a decompiled heapify utility that constructs a binary max-heap from a list of comparable elements.

mbpp_0469.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum profit earned from a maximum of k stock transactions

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum profit earned from a maximum of k stock transactions
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Maximum Profit with K Stock Transactions (Dynamic Programming)
Main goal: Given an array of daily stock prices and an integer n, compute the maximum profit achievable with at most n buy-sell transactions using a 2D dynamic programming table dp[t][d], where dp[t][d] represents the best profit with t transactions up to day d. The recurrence uses dp[t][d] = max(dp[t][d-1], max over m < d of (price[d] - price[m] + dp[t-1][m])), with base cases dp[0][d] = 0 and dp[t][0] = 0. Returns dp[n][last_day].

mbpp_0639.reference_description: Write a function to sum the length of the names of a given array of names after removing the names that start with a lowercase letter.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to sum the length of the names of a given array of names after removing the names that start with a lowercase letter.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Sum lengths of properly capitalized words in a list

Main goal: The sampleNam(List<String>) method iterates through a list of strings and returns the total number of characters in strings that (a) have length greater than 1, (b) start with an uppercase letter, and (c) have all remaining characters lowercase. Essentially, it sums the lengths of words like "Hello" and ignores others. The code uses obfuscated helper methods to perform simple comparisons.

mbpp_0382.reference_description: Write a function to find the number of rotations in a circularly sorted array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the number of rotations in a circularly sorted array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Finds the rotation count by locating the index of the smallest element (the rotation pivot) in a rotated sorted integer array using a binary search. Returns 0 when the array is already sorted (no rotation), or the pivot index otherwise; may return -1 if no pivot is found. Handles circular indexing for mid-neighbor checks.

mbpp_0247.reference_description: Write a function to find the longest palindromic subsequence in the given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the longest palindromic subsequence in the given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Longest Palindromic Subsequence Length Calculator (dynamic programming)

Main goal: Compute the length of the longest palindromic subsequence (LPS) for a given string using a 2D dynamic programming table. The code initializes base cases for substrings of length 1, then fills the table for longer substrings by:
- If the end characters match, dp[i][j] = dp[i+1][j-1] + 2 (or 2 when the length is 2).
- If they don’t match, dp[i][j] = max(dp[i][j-1], dp[i+1][j]).

The final result is dp[0][n-1], the LPS length for the entire string. The helper methods Il, I, and l are simple comparison helpers. Note: the code contains decompiler/no-op artifacts but implements the standard O(n^2) time and space DP for LPS.

mbpp_0306.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum sum of increasing subsequence from prefix till ith index and also including a given kth element which is after i, i.e., k > i .

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum sum of increasing subsequence from prefix till ith index and also including a given kth element which is after i, i.e., k > i .
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MaxSumIncreasingSubseq – a dynamic programming solution to the maximum sum of an increasing subsequence
Main goal: Build a 2D DP table to track sums of increasing subsequences in the input array and return the value stored at dp[n2][n3], effectively computing the MSIS up to a given pair of indices.

mbpp_0689.reference_description: ## write a function to find the minimum number of jumps to reach the end of the array for the given array of integers where each element represents the max number of steps that can be made forward from that element. > indented block > indented block

Description_Simple.reference_text: ## write a function to find the minimum number of jumps to reach the end of the array for the given array of integers where each element represents the max number of steps that can be made forward from that element. > indented block > indented block
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
### Summary_description
MinJumps: Dynamic-programming solution to compute the minimum number of jumps to reach the end of an array.

Goal: Given an array of non-negative integers where each element represents the maximum jump length from that index, compute the smallest number of jumps needed to reach the last index. If the end is unreachable (e.g., an empty array or the first element is 0), it returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. The algorithm uses a DP array where dp[i] stores the minimum jumps to reach index i, initializes dp[0] = 0, and for each position i > 0 it checks all previous positions j < i to see if j can jump to i (j + a[j] >= i) and updates dp[i] = min(dp[i], dp[j] + 1). The result is dp[n-1].

mbpp_0466.reference_description: Write a function to find the peak element in the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the peak element in the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Binary Search Based Peak Finder

Main goal: Locate and return the index of a local peak in an array by recursively checking the middle element; if a neighboring element is larger, narrow the search to that side, otherwise declare the middle element a peak. The algorithm effectively performs a binary-search-like search for a local maximum.

mbpp_0239.reference_description: Write a function to find the number of possible sequences of length n such that each of the next element is greater than or equal to twice of the previous element but less than or equal to m.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the number of possible sequences of length n such that each of the next element is greater than or equal to twice of the previous element but less than or equal to m.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: SequenceCounter
Main goal: Compute a two-parameter count using dynamic programming by filling a (n+1) x (n2+1) table with the recurrence: dp[i][j] = 0 if i == 0 or j == 0 or i < j; dp[i][1] = i; otherwise dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] + dp[i/2][j-1]; and return dp[n][n2].

mbpp_0107.reference_description: Write a java function to count hexadecimal numbers for a given range.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count hexadecimal numbers for a given range.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Counts how many hexadecimal digits among all integers in the inclusive range [n, n2] are digits 10–15 (i.e., A–F). For each number in the range, if it lies between 10 and 15 inclusive, it contributes 1. If it is greater than 15, it is examined digit-by-digit in base-16 by repeatedly taking the remainder modulo 16 and dividing by 16, and each digit that is >= 10 contributes 1 to the total. The function returns the total count of such hex digits across the entire range.

mbpp_0826.reference_description: Write a java function to find the type of triangle from the given sides.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the type of triangle from the given sides.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: TriangleType - Triangle Angle Category Detector

Main goal: Given three side lengths, classify the triangle as right-angled, obtuse-angled, or acute-angled by comparing the squares of the sides (a^2, b^2, c^2) using Pythagorean relations. It uses a set of small helper methods to determine the sign of pairwise comparisons and applies the logic across all three side permutations. Note: There is no validation of triangle inequality or input feasibility.

mbpp_0885.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the two given strings are isomorphic to each other or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the two given strings are isomorphic to each other or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Isomorphic - Two strings areomorphism checker
Main goal: Determine whether two strings are isomorphic by recording, for each character, the list of its positions in each string, then sorting these position-lists by their patterns and comparing the resulting structures to decide if the strings have the same character-position pattern.

mbpp_0121.reference_description: Write a function to find the triplet with sum of the given array

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the triplet with sum of the given array
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Recursive triplet-sum checker
Main goal: Determine whether there exists a combination of exactly three elements from the first n elements of nArray that sums to n2, using a backtracking recursion (include current element and subtract its value from the target, or skip it), with base cases recognizing a successful triplet or pruning conditions.

mbpp_0108.reference_description: Write a function to merge multiple sorted inputs into a single sorted iterator using heap queue algorithm.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to merge multiple sorted inputs into a single sorted iterator using heap queue algorithm.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Merge three lists into one sorted list using a min-heap
Main goal: Sort three input integer lists and merge them into a single ascending list by repeatedly extracting the smallest current element via a PriorityQueue (min-heap) of Node objects that store the value and its originating iterator. Returns a List<Integer> containing all elements in non-decreasing order.

How it works (brief): 
- Each input list is sorted individually. 
- The first element from each non-empty list is put into the heap along with its iterator. 
- While the heap is non-empty, the smallest value is popped, added to the result, and the next value from that list (if any) is pushed onto the heap. 
- Node implements Comparable by value to maintain heap ordering.

Notes: The code uses obfuscated helpers and no-op lines, but the core logic is a standard three-way merge via a min-heap. Time complexity is O(n log k) with k = 3 (effectively O(n)); space complexity is O(k).

mbpp_0570.reference_description: Write a function to remove words from a given array of strings containing a character or string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to remove words from a given array of strings containing a character or string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: RemoveWordsUtil - Filter out words containing forbidden substrings
Main goal: Given a list of lines and a list of forbidden substrings, produce a new list where each line has its words filtered to remove any word that contains any of the forbidden substrings, and then the remaining words are joined back into lines.

mbpp_0181.reference_description: Write a function to find the longest common prefix in the given set of strings.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the longest common prefix in the given set of strings.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Longest Common Prefix Calculator
Main goal: Compute the longest common prefix among a list of strings. It exposes:
- commonPrefixUtil: returns the common prefix of two strings by comparing characters from the start until a mismatch occurs.
- commonPrefix: iteratively applies commonPrefixUtil across an array of strings to obtain the overall common prefix (or an empty string if the input is empty).

mbpp_0231.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum sum in the given right triangle of numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum sum in the given right triangle of numbers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: TriangleMaxSum – in-place dynamic programming for triangle maximum path sum.
Main goal: Compute the maximum total from top to bottom of a triangular array by updating rows in place (edges add their single parent; interior elements take the max of two possible parent sums) and return the largest value found in the last row.

mbpp_0485.reference_description: Write a function to find the largest palindromic number in the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the largest palindromic number in the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: PalindromeUtils
Main goal: Provide utilities to (1) check if an integer is a palindrome (isPalindrome) by comparing digits from the outside in, and (2) find the largest palindrome value in an integer array (largestPalindrome) by sorting the array and scanning from largest to smallest, returning -1 if none. The code uses extra, intentionally obfuscated no-op segments (likely from decompilation).

mbpp_0685.reference_description: Write a java function to find sum of prime numbers between 1 to n.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find sum of prime numbers between 1 to n.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
PrimeSum: Sum of primes up to n
Main goal: Compute the sum of all prime numbers from 2 to n (inclusive) using the Sieve of Eratosthenes, and return that total.

mbpp_0863.reference_description: Write a function to find the length of the longest sub-sequence such that elements in the subsequences are consecutive integers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the length of the longest sub-sequence such that elements in the subsequences are consecutive integers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Longest Consecutive Subsequence Length Calculator

Main goal: Given an integer array and its length, compute the length of the longest run of consecutive integers that appear in the array. The code sorts the array, builds a list of distinct values, then scans that list to count the longest sequence where each element is exactly 1 more than the previous, returning that maximum length. Helper methods are used to perform simple comparisons, but the overall purpose is to find the longest consecutive subsequence length.

mbpp_0397.reference_description: Write a function to find the median of three specific numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the median of three specific numbers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MedianFinder.medianNumbers — Median of three integers

Main goal: Given three integers n, n2, and n3, compute and return the median (the middle value when the three are sorted) using a fixed set of pairwise comparisons. The code uses two helper methods: l(a,b) for a < b and I(a,b) for a > b, and then follows a sequence of conditional branches to select the correct middle value. There are decompiler/obfuscation artifacts sprinkled in, but the core logic implements the standard “median of three” decision process.

mbpp_0526.reference_description: Write a java function to capitalize first and last letters of each word of a given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to capitalize first and last letters of each word of a given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: StringUtil.capitalizeFirstLastLetters

Main goal: Take an input string, convert it to lowercase, split on whitespace into words, and for each word capitalize the first and last letters (single-letter words are fully capitalized; longer words have first and last letters uppercase with the middle kept lowercase). Then rejoin the words with single spaces. If the input is null or empty, return it unchanged. The class also includes small helper methods that wrap simple boolean checks and several no-op artefacts common in decompiled/obfuscated code.

mbpp_0632.reference_description: Write a java function to move all zeroes to the end of the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to move all zeroes to the end of the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Move zeros to the end of the list (preserving non-zero order)
Main goal: The function moveZero takes a List<Integer>, counts how many zeros are present, creates a new list containing all non-zero elements in their original order, then appends the counted number of zeros to the end. The final list has the same non-zero sequence followed by zeros. (The code appears obfuscated with useless no-op statements, but the effective behavior is as described.)

mbpp_0745.reference_description: Write a function to find numbers within a given range where every number is divisible by every digit it contains.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find numbers within a given range where every number is divisible by every digit it contains.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Finds and returns a list of numbers in the inclusive range [n, n2] such that every non-zero digit of the number is a divisor of the number (i.e., the number is divisible by each of its non-zero digits).

mbpp_0971.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum number of segments of lengths a, b and c that can be formed from n.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum number of segments of lengths a, b and c that can be formed from n.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Dynamic Programming to Maximize Segment Count

Main goal: Compute the maximum number of segments (of lengths n2, n3, n4) that sum exactly to the target length n. It uses a 1D DP array where index represents a total length and the value stores the maximum number of segments needed to reach that total. Starting from 0 (0 segments), it iteratively extends reachable totals by adding each segment length, updating the maximum count. Returns -1 if the target length n cannot be formed.

mbpp_0943.reference_description: Write a function to combine two given sorted arrays using heapq module.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to combine two given sorted arrays using heapq module.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code defines a MergeUtils class with a single merge method combineLists that merges two sorted List<Integer> inputs into a new sorted list. It walks both lists with indices, appending the smaller current element from either list (and when equal, prefers the element from the first list) until one list is exhausted, then appends any remaining elements from the other list. Helper methods I and l implement index comparisons used during merging. The result is a non-decreasing sequence containing all elements from both input lists. The code contains some decompiler artifact lines that have no effect.

mbpp_0620.reference_description: Write a function to find the largest subset where each pair is divisible.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the largest subset where each pair is divisible.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Longest Divisible Subset Length (order-based DP)
Main goal: Given an array, compute the size of the largest subset in which every pair of numbers is divisible one by the other (i.e., the numbers form a chain under divisibility). It does a bottom-up dynamic programming pass from the end toward the start, setting dp[i] = 1 + max(dp[j]) over j > i where a[i] divides a[j] or a[j] divides a[i], with dp[n-1] = 1, and finally returns the maximum dp value. The code uses simple divisibility tests and ignores extraneous decompiler artifacts.

mbpp_0054.reference_description: Write a function to sort the given array by using counting sort.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to sort the given array by using counting sort.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
### Title: CountingSort - Counting sort implementation for int arrays (obfuscated/decompiled)

Main goal: Sorts an int[] in ascending order using the counting sort algorithm. It first finds the maximum value in the input, builds a frequency array, counts occurrences of each value, and then writes back the sorted values into the original array, returning it. The code uses small helper methods as obfuscated comparators and contains no-op artifacts typical of decompiled code.

mbpp_0256.reference_description: Write a java function to count the number of prime numbers less than a given non-negative number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count the number of prime numbers less than a given non-negative number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: PrimeCounter: Counts primes below a given n. Main goal: count how many prime numbers are strictly less than n using a naive trial-division test. The countPrimesNums(n) method iterates n3 from 0 up to n-1; for n3 >= 2 it checks divisibility by integers from 2 to n3-1 and increments a counter when no divisor is found, effectively returning the number of primes less than n. Helper methods I, l, ll, Il implement tiny boolean predicates used in the logic; the surrounding odd strings/useless checks are decompiler artifacts and do not affect the result.

mbpp_0597.reference_description: Write a function to find kth element from the given two sorted arrays.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find kth element from the given two sorted arrays.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
KthElementFinder: Merge two sorted arrays and return the k-th element
Goal: Given two sorted int arrays (lengths n and n2), merge them into a single sorted array and return the k-th element (1-based) from that merged array (i.e., element at index k-1). It uses a standard merge procedure with O(n + n2) time and O(n + n2) extra space.

mbpp_0922.reference_description: Write a function to find a pair with the highest product from a given array of integers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find a pair with the highest product from a given array of integers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MaxProductFinder - Find the pair with the maximum product
Main goal: Given an int[] nArray, return the two elements whose product is the largest. If the input is null or has fewer than two elements, return null. The method exhaustively checks all unordered pairs (i < j), keeps the pair with the greatest long product, and returns them as a two-element int[].

mbpp_0476.reference_description: Write a java function to find the sum of the largest and smallest value in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the sum of the largest and smallest value in a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Sum of Array Minimum and Maximum
Main goal: Given a non-null, non-empty integer array, compute and return the sum of its smallest and largest values. The implementation validates input, iterates once to track the current minimum and maximum, and returns min + max. It throws IllegalArgumentException if the array is null or empty.

mbpp_0588.reference_description: Write a java function to find the difference between largest and smallest value in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the difference between largest and smallest value in a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: BigDiff - Maximum-Minimum Difference

Main goal: Given a non-null, non-empty int array, compute the difference between its largest and smallest elements by a single pass (tracking min and max). It validates input and throws an exception if the array is null or empty.

mbpp_0415.reference_description: Write a java function to find a pair with highest product from a given array of integers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find a pair with highest product from a given array of integers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MaxProduct - Find the pair with the maximum product
Main goal: Given an array of integers, find and return the two elements whose product is the largest among all distinct pairs. The method maxProduct validates input (non-null and at least two elements), then iterates over all pairs (i < j), tracks the pair with the largest product, and returns it as a two-element array. Helper methods perform simple comparisons.

mbpp_0918.reference_description: Write a function to count coin change.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to count coin change.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: CoinChange — Dynamic programming solution for counting coin combinations
Main goal: Given an array of coin values nArray (length n) and a target sum n2, compute how many unordered combinations (unlimited coins of each type) can sum to n2. It uses a 2D DP table where dp[i][j] represents the number of ways to make sum i using the first j+1 coin types. Base case dp[0][j] = 1 for all j, and the recurrence is dp[i][j] = dp[i - coin_j][j] + dp[i][j-1], yielding the result dp[n2][n-1].

mbpp_0342.reference_description: Write a function to find the smallest range that includes at-least one element from each of the given arrays.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the smallest range that includes at-least one element from each of the given arrays.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Smallest range containing at least one element from each list

Main goal: Given a list of sorted integer lists, compute and return the smallest possible range [low, high] such that every input list contributes at least one value within that range. The code uses a min-heap (PriorityQueue) of Node objects (value, list index, position within the list) to always pull the current smallest value, while tracking the current maximum among the chosen elements. It initializes the heap with the first element from each list, expands by taking the next element from the list of the polled node, updates the maximum, and records the best (nArray) range whenever the current window [min, max] is smaller. The process stops when any list is exhausted, returning the best range found.

mbpp_0531.reference_description: Write a function to find minimum number of coins that make a given value.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find minimum number of coins that make a given value.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
CoinChange: Recursive Minimum Coin Change Solver

Main goal: Compute the smallest number of coins needed to sum to a given target amount n2 using the denominations provided in nArray[0..n-1], via a naive recursive search. It returns Integer.MAX_VALUE if no combination can achieve the target.

How it works (brief): Base case — if n2 == 0, return 0. Otherwise, for each coin value nArray[i] with i < n and value <= n2, recursively solve for the remaining amount (n2 - nArray[i]); if the recursive result is valid (not Integer.MAX_VALUE) and yields a smaller total (subresult + 1) than the current best, update the best. After trying all coins, return the best. Helper methods implement simple relational checks (n < m, n <= m, n == 0, n != m). The extra lines in the decompiled code are artifacts and do not alter the core logic.

mbpp_0702.reference_description: Write a function to find the minimum number of elements that should be removed such that amax-amin<=k.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the minimum number of elements that should be removed such that amax-amin<=k.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Minimum Removals to Fit Values Within a Fixed Range

Main goal: Given an array of integers, compute the smallest number of elements to remove so that the remaining elements can be contained within an interval of width n2 (i.e., max - min <= n2). The code sorts the array, then for each starting index uses a binary-search helper to find the farthest ending index that satisfies the difference condition, and keeps track of the minimal removals as total elements minus the length of the best window.

What the key parts do:
- findInd(value, leftIndex, rightLimit, maxDiff, arr): performs a binary search to find the last index k in the range (leftIndex, rightLimit) such that arr[k] - value <= maxDiff. Returns -1 if no such index exists.
- removals(arr, n, d): sorts the array, then for each start index i, finds the farthest end index j using findInd for which arr[j] - arr[i] <= d. If such j exists, updates the minimum removals as n - (j - i + 1). Returns the smallest removals found.
- Helper methods I, l, Il are tiny comparisons used by the logic (e.g., I checks n < m, l checks n <= m, Il checks n != m). The odd string-length lines are decompiler artifacts and have no effect on logic.

In short, the code implements a binary-search-enhanced two-pointer technique to determine the minimum number of elements to remove so that the remaining values fit within a contiguous value range of size at most n2.

mbpp_0448.reference_description: Write a function to calculate the sum of perrin numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to calculate the sum of perrin numbers.

The code handles n=0,1,2 directly (3, 3, and 5 respectively); for n>2 it iteratively generates successive Perrin terms and accumulates them into the total, returning the final sum.

mbpp_0853.reference_description: Write a java function to find sum of odd factors of a number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find sum of odd factors of a number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code implements sumOfOddFactors(n): it computes the sum of all positive odd divisors of n (i.e., the sigma function of the odd part of n). It first strips all factors of 2 from n, then factorizes the remaining odd part by trial division (3,5,7,... up to sqrt). For each odd prime p with exponent e, it multiplies the running result by (1 + p + p^2 + ... + p^e). If a remaining factor > 1 remains after the loop, it multiplies by (1 + that factor). The final product is the sum of all odd divisors of the original input. Note: if n is 0, the code would loop indefinitely.

If e > 0, it adds to a running total the largest k such that k(k+1)/2 <= e (i.e., the number of triangular numbers not exceeding e). After processing all d, if a leftover factor remains (n > 1), it adds 1. The helper methods implement basic comparisons used in the loops.

mbpp_0020.reference_description: Write a function to check if the given number is woodball or not.

Main goal: Given a long input l, determine whether it satisfies a specific Woodall-number–related condition. The method isWoodall behaves as follows: it immediately returns false for even numbers, returns true when l == 1, and for odd l > 1 it sets l to l+1 and then repeatedly, while l is even, halves l and increments a counter. If at any step the counter equals the halved value, it returns true; if the halving loop ends with l becoming odd, it returns false. mbpp_0506.reference_description: Write a function to calculate the permutation coefficient of given p(n, k).

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to calculate the permutation coefficient of given p(n, k).
Description_Simple.comparison_text: <Summary_description>The code implements a dynamic programming routine in PermutationCoefficient.permutationCoefficient(n, n2) that builds a 2D table lArray and returns lArray[n][n2]. The recurrence used is l[n][k] = l[n-1][k] + k * l[n-1][k-1], which matches the standard recurrence for Stirling numbers of the second kind, with a nonstandard base case: l[n][0] is set to 1 for all n (instead of 0 for n>0). The method initializes l[0][0] = 1 and fills the table for 0 <= n2' <= min(n, n2). Helper methods Il, I, and l implement bounds checks (<, <=) and the test n == 0, respectively. The code also contains several no-op artifacts and decompiler quirks (e.g., string-length checks). In intent, it aims to compute a permutation/partition coefficient (akin to S(n, k)), but due to the base case it yields incorrect values for n > 0. The function returns the computed value for (n, n2).
