Title: Top-N Largest Elements Extractor (LargestN.larg_nnum)
Main goal: Given a list of comparable elements and an integer n, return a List containing the n largest elements from the input in descending order. It uses a min-heap (priority queue) to keep track of the current top-n as it iterates: it fills the heap with the first n elements, then for each subsequent element, if it is larger than the smallest in the heap, it replaces that smallest. After processing, it converts the heap to a list and sorts it in descending order before returning. (Note: assumes n > 0 and elements are mutually comparable.)

mbpp_0029.reference_description: Write a java function to find the element occurring odd number of times.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the element occurring odd number of times.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code implements getOddOccurrence(int[] nArray, int n) which scans the first n elements of the array and returns the first value whose total number of occurrences among those n elements is odd; if no such value exists, it returns -1. It uses a nested loop to count occurrences of each candidate element (comparing values with a helper l), and a parity check (Il) to determine odd counts.

mbpp_0034.reference_description: Write a java function to find the missing number in a sorted array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the missing number in a sorted array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Binary search to find a single missing number in 1..n
Main goal: Given a sorted array of length n-1 containing all integers from 1 to n except one missing, the code uses binary search to locate and return that missing number. It checks at mid whether the value equals its expected position (mid+1) and whether the previous element matches its expected value; if so, the missing number is mid+1. Otherwise it narrows the search to the left or right half. If no missing number is found, it returns -1. The helper methods implement simple equality/inequality/comparison used during the search.

mbpp_0130.reference_description: Write a function to find the item with maximum frequency in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the item with maximum frequency in a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Maximum-frequency element finder for a list
Main goal: Build a frequency map of elements in a list and return the Map.Entry<T, Integer> corresponding to the element that occurs most often (or null if the list is empty). The code first counts occurrences with a HashMap, then iterates the map to select the entry with the largest count.

mbpp_0659.reference_description: Write a java function to print duplicants from array of integers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to print duplicants from array of integers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Response:
Title: DuplicateFinder
Main goal: Given an int array, it returns a list of values that appear more than once, including each duplicated value only once in the result. It does this by exhaustively comparing every pair of elements and adding a value to the output if it finds a second occurrence and that value hasn’t already been added.

mbpp_0207.reference_description: Write a function to count the longest repeating subsequences such that the two subsequences don’t have same string characters at same positions.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to count the longest repeating subsequences such that the two subsequences don’t have same string characters at same positions.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Computes the length of the longest repeating subsequence (LRS) of a string using a dynamic programming table dp[i][j]. For prefixes of length i and j, if characters at i-1 and j-1 match and i != j, it sets dp[i][j] = 1 + dp[i-1][j-1]; otherwise it uses dp[i][j] = max(dp[i][j-1], dp[i-1][j]). The result is dp[n][n]. The code includes helper methods for character equality and index comparisons, and contains some extraneous no-op statements that do not affect the core DP logic.

mbpp_0604.reference_description: Write a function to reverse words in a given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to reverse words in a given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: ReverseWords: reversing the order of whitespace-delimited words in a string

Main goal: Given a string, reverse the order of its words (split on whitespace) and join them with single spaces; if the input is null or empty, return it unchanged.

Summary_description:
The method reverseWords splits the input on one or more whitespace characters, then rebuilds a string by appending tokens from the end to the start with spaces in between, effectively reversing word order. It returns the resulting string, or the original input if it is null or empty. The code uses small helper methods for null, nonzero, and non-negative checks, and contains decompilation artifacts that do not alter overall behavior.

mbpp_0304.reference_description: Write a java function to find element at a given index after number of rotations.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find element at a given index after number of rotations.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Obfuscated interval-driven index transformer to select an element

Main goal: Given an array nArray and a list of index intervals nArray2 where each pair [left, right] represents a range, compute the final element to return by starting with an index n2 and processing the intervals from the end to the start. For each interval [n4, n5]:
- If n4 <= n2 <= n5, then if n2 == n4 set n2 = n5, else decrement n2 by 1.
After all intervals are processed, return nArray[n2].

Notes:
- ll checks equality (n == n2)
- Il checks n >= n2
- l checks n <= n2
- I checks n >= 0
Time complexity: O(m) where m is the number of intervals; Space: O(1)

mbpp_0366.reference_description: Write a java function to find the largest product of the pair of adjacent elements from a given array of integers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the largest product of the pair of adjacent elements from a given array of integers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Maximum product of adjacent elements
Goal: Given a non-null int array with at least two elements, return the largest product of any two consecutive elements. The code validates input, initializes the maximum with the product of the first two elements, then scans all adjacent pairs to update the maximum. Time complexity is O(n) and space complexity is O(1).

mbpp_0275.reference_description: Write a java function to find the position of the last removed element from the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the position of the last removed element from the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Ceiling-divide and rightmost-maximum index finder

Main goal: The getPosition method takes an int array and two integers (n and n2). It first replaces each array element with the ceiling of element/n2 (for nonnegative elements; a small amount of dead/decompiler noise is present). Then it scans the transformed array from the end to the start to find the index of the rightmost maximum value, and returns that index plus one (i.e., a 1-based position). If the input length is 0, it returns 0. There is a lot of obfuscated/decompiled boilerplate (e.g., the string-length checks) that do nothing functionally.

mbpp_0192.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether a string has atleast one letter and one number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether a string has atleast one letter and one number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Response:
Title: StringChecker.checkString
Main goal: Check if a string contains at least one letter and at least one digit; return true if both are present, otherwise false.

mbpp_0842.reference_description: Write a function to find the number which occurs for odd number of times in the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the number which occurs for odd number of times in the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: First odd-occurrence finder in a subarray
Main goal: Given an int array and a length n, locate and return the first element (among indices 0..n-1) that appears an odd number of times in those n elements; if none exists, return -1. It uses a naive O(n^2) approach with nested loops and small helper methods for equality, comparison, and parity.

mbpp_0510.reference_description: Write a function to find the number of subsequences having product smaller than k for the given non negative array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the number of subsequences having product smaller than k for the given non negative array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Implements a dynamic programming solution to count subsequences of a given integer array whose product equals a target value n. It maintains a 2D DP table where dp[x][i] represents the number of subsequences using the first i elements that produce product x. For each element a[i], if a[i] <= x (and positive), it updates dp[x][i] by adding dp[x / a[i]][i-1] + 1 (i.e., using the element to extend subsequences that form x / a[i], plus the single-element subsequence when appropriate). The result returned is dp[n][n2].

mbpp_0498.reference_description: Write a java function to find gcd of two positive integers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find gcd of two positive integers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: GCD.gcd - Simple greatest common divisor calculator

Main goal: Compute the greatest common divisor of two integers. It first returns n2 if n is a multiple of n2; otherwise it searches downward from n2/2 to 1 to find the largest value that divides both n and n2, effectively yielding gcd(n, n2). It uses two helpers: I(n) checks for zero and l(n) checks for positive values.

mbpp_0577.reference_description: Write a java function to find the last digit in factorial of a given number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the last digit in factorial of a given number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Summary_description
Title: Last digit of factorial
Main goal: Given a non-negative integer n, return the last digit of n! (the factorial). It handles specific small values with exact results (0 -> 1, 1 or 2 -> n, 3 -> 6, 4 -> 4) and returns 0 for all n >= 5, since those factorials end in 0.

mbpp_0188.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the given number can be represented by product of two squares or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the given number can be represented by product of two squares or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: ProdSquareChecker — Checks if a number is a square of a composite number
Main goal: Determine whether the input n can be written as n = (a*b)^2 with integers a, b ≥ 2 (i.e., n is a perfect square whose square root is composite). The code searches for factors a and b using nested loops and returns true if such a factorization exists; otherwise it returns false.

mbpp_0183.reference_description: Write a function to count all the distinct pairs having a difference of k in any array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to count all the distinct pairs having a difference of k in any array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: CountPairs - Pairs with a given difference
Main goal: In countPairs, iterate over all pairs (i, j) with i < j in the input array and count how many pairs have an absolute difference equal to the second parameter (n2).

mbpp_0916.reference_description: Write a function to find if there is a triplet in the array whose sum is equal to a given value.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find if there is a triplet in the array whose sum is equal to a given value.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: TripletSum - Brute-force triplet sum checker

Main goal: Determine whether there exist three distinct elements in the given array whose sum equals the specified target (n2). It uses three nested loops to try all i < j < k triplets and returns true if any triplet sums to n2; otherwise, it returns false.Helper methods perform simple equality and bound checks; the approach is O(n^3).

mbpp_0899.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether an array can be sorted or not by picking only the corner elements.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether an array can be sorted or not by picking only the corner elements.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
The code defines a CornerSortChecker with a static check method that iterates from index 1 up to n-1 of the input array. It would return false only if it finds an increasing adjacent pair (a[i] > a[i-1]) and a flag n2 is already set to 1; otherwise it attempts to set that flag when a[i] - a[i] < 0, which is impossible since a[i] - a[i] is always 0. Therefore, the flag never becomes 1, and the method always returns true (for valid indices) after completing the loop. In short, the checker is effectively a no-op due to a decompilation artifact.

Auxiliary methods implement simple comparisons:
- Il(n, n2): true if n == n2
- I(n, n2): true if n < n2
- ll(n): true if n < 0
- l(n): true if n > 0

Overall goal (intended): detect a specific "corner" pattern in the array, but the current logic never triggers the false outcome because the flag can never be set.

mbpp_0552.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether a given sequence is linear or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether a given sequence is linear or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: SequenceUtils seqLinear - Arithmetic progression detector
Main goal: Determine whether an int array forms a linear (arithmetic) sequence. If the input is null or has fewer than 2 elements, or any consecutive difference differs from the initial difference, it returns "Non Linear Sequence"; otherwise it returns "Linear Sequence". Uses small helper methods (l, I, Il) that perform simple comparisons (appearing obfuscated).

mbpp_0672.reference_description: Write a function to find maximum of three numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find maximum of three numbers.

It uses a private helper I(int a, int b) to check if a >= b and selects the maximum via conditional branches. The extra no-op statements are decompilation artifacts and have no effect on the logic.

mbpp_0227.reference_description: Write a function to find minimum of three numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find minimum of three numbers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MinOfThree - find the smallest of three integers
Main goal: Provide a simple function minOfThree(int n, int n2, int n3) that returns the smallest of the three inputs by using a small helper I(int a, int b) that checks a <= b. It returns n if n is <= both others; else returns n2 if n2 is <= both others; otherwise returns n3.

mbpp_0438.reference_description: Write a function to count bidirectional tuple pairs.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to count bidirectional tuple pairs.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Bidirectional Edge Pair Counter

Main goal: Given a 2D int array where each row represents an edge as [u, v], the code counts how many pairs of edges (i, j) with i < j satisfy the condition v_i == u_j (i.e., the end of the first edge matches the start of the second edge). It returns that count as a string. Helper methods l and I perform simple comparisons (equality and less-than). The surrounding seemingly obfuscated blocks are no-ops and do not affect the core counting logic.

mbpp_0172.reference_description: Write a function to find the occurence of characters 'std' in the given string 1. array item 1. array item 1. array item 2. array item 2. array item 2. array item

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the occurence of characters 'std' in the given string 1. array item 1. array item 1. array item 2. array item 2. array item 2. array item

It iterates character by character up to length-3, checks for 's' (115), 't' (116), and 'd' (100) in consecutive positions, and increments a counter. Helper methods perform simple equality and <= comparisons. (Note: there are decompiler-generated no-op lines that do not affect the logic.)

mbpp_0191.reference_description: Write a function to check whether the given month name contains 30 days or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check whether the given month name contains 30 days or not.

mbpp_0481.reference_description: Write a function to determine if there is a subset of the given set with sum equal to the given sum.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to determine if there is a subset of the given set with sum equal to the given sum.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Response:
Title: Subset Sum Recursive Solver

Main goal: Determine if there exists a subset of the first n elements of nArray whose sum equals n2. The code uses a recursive approach with base cases (target sum 0 -> true; no elements left -> false), skips the last element when it is larger than the target, and otherwise explores two possibilities: excluding or including the last element (reducing the target by that element's value). The helper methods are simple boolean checks used to drive this logic (obfuscated in the decompiled version).

mbpp_0663.reference_description: Write a function to find the largest possible value of k such that k modulo x is y.

mbpp_0876.reference_description: Write a java function to find lcm of two positive integers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find lcm of two positive integers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Obfuscated LCM brute-force calculator
Main goal: Compute the least common multiple (LCM) of two integers by iterating upward from the larger of the two until a number divisible by both is found. It uses two helpers: I checks if the first argument is greater than the second (to decide the starting candidate) and l checks if a value is zero (used to test divisibility). The code is written in a deliberately obfuscated/decompiled style, but its intended function is a naive LCM finder.

mbpp_0520.reference_description: Write a function to find the lcm of the given array elements.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the lcm of the given array elements.

LCMCalculator — Computes the least common multiple

Main goal: Provide methods to compute the LCM of two integers (findLcm) and of an array of integers (getLcm) by using the Euclidean algorithm to compute gcd and then LCM = a*b/gcd; includes small helper methods for comparisons (Il, I) and non-zero check (l), with some decompiler-inserted no-op code.

mbpp_0843.reference_description: Write a function to find the nth super ugly number from a given prime array of size k using heap queue algorithm.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the nth super ugly number from a given prime array of size k using heap queue algorithm.

Title: Min-Heap-based nth Super Ugly Number Calculator
Main goal: Compute the nth super ugly number given a set of primes (nArray) by generating the sequence with a priority queue. It starts from 1, maintains for each prime its next multiple (via an index into the current list), repeatedly takes the smallest candidate, appends it if it's new, updates that prime's candidate, and continues until the nth number is produced.

mbpp_0961.reference_description: Write a function to convert a roman numeral to an integer.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to convert a roman numeral to an integer.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: RomanConverter - Roman numeral to integer
Main goal: Convert a Roman numeral string to its integer value by mapping symbols (I,V,X,L,C,D,M) to their numeric values and applying the standard subtractive rule (when a smaller value precedes a larger one). It uses a hashmap, iterates left-to-right, and adjusts the sum by adding the current value or current value minus twice the previous value. Includes helper methods for simple comparisons and contains decompiler artifacts (dead/no-op code).

mbpp_0018.reference_description: Write a function to remove characters from the first string which are present in the second string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to remove characters from the first string which are present in the second string.

Title: Java StringUtil: ASCII-based string/char utilities

Main goal: Provide basic utilities to convert between String and char[] and to remove characters from a string that appear in another "dirty" string by building a 256-entry frequency map of the dirty characters and filtering the original string accordingly.

mbpp_0364.reference_description: Write a function to find the number of flips required to make the given binary string a sequence of alternate characters.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the number of flips required to make the given binary string a sequence of alternate characters.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:

Main goal: Given a string of '0' and '1', compute the smallest number of bit flips needed to transform it into an alternating pattern (0101... or 1010...). It does this by counting mismatches for both possible starting characters and returning the minimum.

mbpp_0911.reference_description: Write a function to compute maximum product of three numbers of a given array of integers using heap queue algorithm.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to compute maximum product of three numbers of a given array of integers using heap queue algorithm.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Maximum product of three numbers using two heaps

Main goal: Compute the maximum product obtainable from any three elements of the input array. It uses two priority queues: a min-heap of size up to 3 to keep the three largest numbers, and a max-heap of size up to 2 to keep the two smallest numbers. After processing, it considers two candidates—the product of the three largest numbers and the product of the largest number with the two smallest numbers (to handle negative values)—and returns the larger one.

mbpp_0179.reference_description: Write a function to find if the given number is a keith number or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find if the given number is a keith number or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code implements KeithNumberChecker with a method isNumKeith(int n). It collects the digits of n, then builds a sequence in which each new term is the sum of the previous d terms, where d is the number of digits of n. It keeps appending terms until a term is >= n. If the term equals n, it returns true (n is a Keith number); otherwise it returns false.

mbpp_0815.reference_description: Write a function to sort the given array without using any sorting algorithm. the given array consists of only 0, 1, and 2.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to sort the given array without using any sorting algorithm. the given array consists of only 0, 1, and 2.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: SortByDNF — In-place Dutch National Flag partition for 0s, 1s, and others
Main goal: Reorder an int[] so that all 0s come first, all 1s come next, and all other values appear at the end, using a single three-pointer pass (low, mid, high) in-place.

mbpp_0541.reference_description: Write a function to find if the given number is abundant or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find if the given number is abundant or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code defines a class AbundantNumber with two main functions: getSum(n) computes the sum of proper divisors of n (by checking divisors up to sqrt(n) and adding divisor pairs, then subtracting n to exclude the number itself), and checkAbundant(n) determines if n is abundant by checking if getSum(n) > n. It uses a few tiny helper methods (I, Il, ll, l) as obfuscated/simple predicates.

mbpp_0832.reference_description: Write a function to extract the maximum numeric value from a string by using regex.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to extract the maximum numeric value from a string by using regex.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Maximum numeric value extractor

Main goal: Finds and returns the largest non-negative integer present as contiguous digits in the input string; if no numbers are found, it throws an IllegalArgumentException.

Functions:
- extractMax(String): scans the string for digit runs using regex \d+, tracks the maximum value, and throws if none are found.
- l(int n, int n2): helper that returns true if the first argument is greater than the second (used to update the max).
- I(int n): helper that returns true if n is non-zero (controls the loop continuation).
- Il(int n): helper that returns true if n is zero (detects no numbers found to throw the exception).

mbpp_0603.reference_description: Write a function to get a lucid number smaller than or equal to n.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to get a lucid number smaller than or equal to n.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Ludic Numbers Sieve: Compute the first n Ludic numbers.
Main goal: Generate the first n Ludic numbers using a sieve-like process: start with a list [1, 2, ..., n], then repeatedly take the current Ludic number from the list and remove every nth remaining element from the list, adjusting for index shifts, until the process finishes, and return the resulting list.

How it works:
- getLudic(n) builds an initial list of integers from 1 to n.
- It then iterates to determine Ludic numbers: n3 is taken as the element at index n2; starting from index n2 + n3, it removes elements at positions spaced by n3, accounting for shifting indices (n4 += n3 - 1 after each removal).
- The loop uses helper methods:
  - I(n, n2) checks n <= n2
  - Il(n, n2) checks n < n2
  - l(n, n2) checks n != n2
- The extra "" .length() calls and if (null == null) blocks are just no-ops used to obfuscate the code and do not affect the algorithm.
- Returns the list of Ludic numbers found (up to the requested count).

mbpp_0711.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the product of digits of a number at even and odd places is equal or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the product of digits of a number at even and odd places is equal or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Response:
Title: Product of digits in odd vs even positions equality
Main goal: The method productEqual(n) checks whether the product of digits in odd positions (from the least significant digit, position 1) equals the product of digits in even positions, for integers n with at least two digits (n >= 10). It returns true if the two products are equal, otherwise false.

mbpp_0571.reference_description: Write a function to find maximum possible sum of disjoint pairs for the given array of integers and a number k.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find maximum possible sum of disjoint pairs for the given array of integers and a number k.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Maximize sum of disjoint pairs with adjacent-element difference < K
Main goal: Sort the input array and compute the maximum total sum obtainable by selecting non-overlapping pairs where the two numbers in each pair differ by less than K. The algorithm uses dynamic programming: after sorting, for i from 1 to n-1, if a[i] - a[i-1] < K then dp[i] = max(dp[i-1], dp[i-2] + a[i] + a[i-1]); otherwise dp[i] = dp[i-1]. The final result is dp[n-1]. (The code includes some decompiler artifacts that do not affect the logic.)

mbpp_0936.reference_description: Write a function to re-arrange the given tuples based on the given ordered array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to re-arrange the given tuples based on the given ordered array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: ReArrangeTuples takes a list of key-value pairs (as SimpleEntry<K,V>) and a separate list of keys. It first builds a map from the input pairs, then iterates over the second list of keys and, for each key that exists in the map, appends a new SimpleEntry(pointing to that key and its mapped value) to the result. The returned list contains only those keys from the second list that were present in the initial pairs, in the order of list2.

mbpp_0472.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the given array contains consecutive numbers or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the given array contains consecutive numbers or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: ConsecutiveChecker validates a consecutive integer sequence
Main goal: Given a list of integers, determine if the list forms a complete, gapless consecutive sequence from its minimum to its maximum (no duplicates, no missing numbers). It does this by computing min and max, sorting the list, ensuring size equals max−min+1, and checking that each element equals min + index; returns true if all checks pass, false otherwise.

mbpp_0136.reference_description: Write a function to calculate electricity bill.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to calculate electricity bill.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Calculates the total bill for a given usage n using a four-tier pricing scheme. The tiers are: (1) n < 50: 2.6 per unit plus a fixed 25; (2) 50 ≤ n ≤ 100: 130 base + 3.25*(n-50) plus fixed 35; (3) 101 ≤ n ≤ 200: 292.5 base + 5.26*(n-100) plus fixed 45; (4) n > 200: 818.5 base + 8.45*(n-200) plus fixed 75. The function returns the sum of the tiered per-unit cost and the fixed charge. Helper methods implement the comparisons (n < 50 and n ≤ 100 / n ≤ 200). There are decompiler artifacts (e.g., unnecessary "" .length() checks) that do not affect behavior. Boundaries between tiers introduce discontinuities due to the specific piecewise formulas.

mbpp_0140.reference_description: Write a function to extract elements that occur singly in the given tuple array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to extract elements that occur singly in the given tuple array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: ExtractSingly — gather unique elements from a list of lists in first-appearance order
Main goal: Given a List<List<T>> it returns a List<T> containing each distinct element encountered while iterating, preserving the order of their first appearance across all inner lists. It uses a HashSet to track seen items and skips duplicates. The surrounding obfuscated statements are no-ops and do not affect the outcome.

mbpp_0316.reference_description: Write a function to find the index of the last occurrence of a given number in a sorted array.

mbpp_0195.reference_description: Write a java function to find the first position of an element in a sorted array.

Main goal: Find the smallest index at which the target value n occurs in the sorted array nArray of length n2, or return -1 if the value is not present. The method first performs a standard binary search over indices [0, n2-1], and when it encounters an element equal to n, it records that index and continues searching left to ensure the first occurrence is returned. Helper methods Il, I, and l implement the <, <=, and > comparisons used during the search.

mbpp_0836.reference_description: Write a function to find length of the subarray having maximum sum.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find length of the subarray having maximum sum.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
<Summary_description>
The code implements a Kadane-like algorithm to compute the length of the contiguous subarray with the maximum sum. It iterates once through the input array, maintaining:
- current sum (n2) and its start index (n5)
- best sum found so far (n) and its start (n3) and end (n4) indices

Whenever the updated current sum exceeds the best sum, it updates the best sum and records the corresponding subarray boundaries. If the current sum becomes negative, it resets the current sum to zero and moves the potential start to the next index. At the end, it returns the length of the best subarray as n4 - n3 + 1. Helper methods I(int, int) and l(int) are simple comparisons used by the logic. Overall complexity is O(n) time and O(1) extra space.

mbpp_0325.reference_description: Write a java function to find the minimum number of squares whose sum is equal to a given number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the minimum number of squares whose sum is equal to a given number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Minimal number of perfect squares summing to n (recursive search)

Main goal: Compute the smallest count of perfect square numbers that sum to a given integer n.

What it does:
- getMinSquares(n) returns the minimal number of squares needed to sum to n.
- Base case: if n <= 3, returns n (since 1^2 + … equals n for small n).
- Otherwise, it tries all square numbers n3^2 with n3 starting at 1 and increasing while n3^2 <= n, recursively solving for the remainder (n - n3^2) and adding 1 for the used square, keeping the minimum result.
- Uses two tiny helpers I and l for simple comparisons (n <= n2 and n > n2 respectively). The rest of the code consists of obfuscated/no-op statements typical of decompiled output.

In essence, it performs a recursive search to find the minimum number of squares whose sum is n (an exponential-time solution without memoization).

mbpp_0974.reference_description: Write a function to find the minimum total path sum in the given triangle.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the minimum total path sum in the given triangle.

Title: Minimum Path Sum in a Matrix (down or down-right)

Main goal: Compute the smallest possible sum along a path from the top-left to the bottom-right of a rectangular matrix (represented as List<List<Integer>>), where each move can go either down or diagonally down-right. It uses a bottom-up dynamic programming approach with a 1D array: initialize the array with the bottom row values, then for each upper row update dp[j] = value_at(i,j) + min(dp[j], dp[j+1]); finally return dp[0] as the minimal path sum. The helper methods I and l perform simple boundary checks.

mbpp_0701.reference_description: Write a function to find the equilibrium index of the given array.

It does this by first summing all elements to get the total, then iterating while maintaining a running left sum and a right sum derived by subtracting the current element from the total, and returning the index when left and right sums match.

mbpp_0047.reference_description: Write a java function to find the last digit when factorial of a divides factorial of b.

The private methods I, l, Il are simple, obfuscated comparisons (n == n2, n >= n2, n <= n2). The extra no-op lines are artifacts of decompilation and do not affect logic.

mbpp_0225.reference_description: Write a java function to find the minimum element in a sorted and rotated array.

Response:
Title: Find minimum in rotated sorted array (with duplicates) using binary search
Main goal: Implement a binary-search style method (findMin) to locate and return the minimum value in a rotated sorted array that may contain duplicates. It maintains a search window [n, n2], computes a middle index, and compares array[mid] with array[n2]:
- if mid > last -> search right half (n = mid + 1)
- if mid < last -> search left half (n2 = mid)
- if mid == last -> shrink the right boundary (n2--)
The loop ends when n == n2, and the minimum value is returned as array[n2]. Helper methods l, I, Il implement equality, less-than, and greater-than comparisons. There are additional no-op statements inserted by the decompiler that have no effect on logic.

mbpp_0357.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum element of all the given tuple records.

It does this in-place by first copying non-zero values to the front, then filling the rest with zeros, and finally returning the same array.
Key functions:
- reOrder(int[]): performs the in-place transformation.
- I(int, int): helper that checks if the first argument is less than the second (loop boundary).
- l(int): helper that checks if a value is non-zero.

mbpp_0384.reference_description: Write a java function to find the frequency of the smallest value in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the frequency of the smallest value in a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Frequency of smallest element in an array
Main goal: Compute how many times the smallest value occurs in the given integer array by scanning it, tracking the current minimum and its count, and returning that count.

mbpp_0489.reference_description: Write a java function to find the frequency of the largest value in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the frequency of the largest value in a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Frequency of the Largest Element in a Prefix of an Array
Main goal: Compute how many times the maximum value occurs among the first n elements of nArray. It iterates through the array, keeps track of the current maximum and its frequency, resets the frequency when a new larger value is found, and increments the count when encountering values equal to the current maximum. Returns the frequency.

mbpp_0546.reference_description: Write a function to find the last occurrence of a character in a string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the last occurrence of a character in a string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: LastOccurrence.lastOccurrenceChar

Main goal: Find the 1-based position (index + 1) of the last occurrence of a given character in a string, returning null if the character does not occur. It iterates through the string, tracks the last matching index, and returns that index plus one. It uses small helper methods for equality and less-than checks, though these are just obfuscated wrappers. Note: decompilation artifacts introduce stray no-op lines, but the core behavior is as described.

mbpp_0627.reference_description: Write a java function to find the smallest missing number from the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the smallest missing number from the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Binary-search-based first-missing-number finder
Goal: Given a sorted array of distinct nonnegative integers, return the smallest nonnegative integer not present in the array by locating the first index i where a[i] != i using a recursive binary search.
Notes: The method findFirstMissing uses index bounds (n, n2). Base cases: if n > n2, return n2+1; if a[n] != n, return n. Otherwise, compare a[mid] with mid: if equal, search right half; if not, search left half. Helpers Il, I, and l are simple equality/ordering predicates.

mbpp_0557.reference_description: Write a function to toggle characters case in a string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to toggle characters case in a string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: StringUtils.toggleString

Main goal: Implement a method toggleString that takes a string and returns a new string with the case of each alphabetic character flipped (uppercase to lowercase and vice versa), while leaving non-letter characters unchanged. It builds the result with a StringBuilder as it iterates through each character, applying a simple case-toggle rule using Character.isUpperCase/isLowerCase. The code includes some decompilation artifacts (nonsensical calls and dead branches) that do not affect the core behavior. Helper methods I and l are trivial: I(n,n2) checks n < n2, and l(n) checks n != 0.

mbpp_0559.reference_description: Write a function to find the largest sum of contiguous subarray in the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the largest sum of contiguous subarray in the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MaxSubArray - Obfuscated Kadane-style maximum subarray sum

Main goal: Compute the maximum subarray sum for the first n elements of the given int array using a Kadane-like approach. It tracks a running sum (n3) and the best sum found so far (n2); if the running sum becomes negative, it resets to zero, and if the running sum surpasses the best sum, the best sum is updated. The helper methods implement simple comparisons: I(a,b) checks a < b, and l(x) checks x < 0. The extra seemingly-no-op statements are artifacts from decompilation and do not alter the algorithm.

mbpp_0681.reference_description: Write a java function to find the smallest prime divisor of a number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the smallest prime divisor of a number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Smallest divisor finder for integers
Main goal: The code returns the smallest non-trivial divisor of an integer n (i.e., its smallest factor). If n is even it returns 2; otherwise it checks odd divisors from 3 up to sqrt(n) and returns the first found divisor. If none is found, it returns n (indicating n is prime). Edge cases: n = 0 yields 2 due to the even check; n = 1 returns 1. The implementation uses obfuscated helper methods and contains no-op lines typical of decompiled code.

mbpp_0903.reference_description: Write a java function to count the total unset bits from 1 to n.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count the total unset bits from 1 to n.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: BitUtils.countUnsetBits

Main goal: Implement countUnsetBits(n) to sum the number of zero bits in the binary representations of all integers from 1 to n (excluding leading zeros). It iterates each number i from 1 to n and for each i counts how many bits in its minimal binary form are 0, returning the total. Helper methods perform simple comparisons and bit tests used by the loops.

mbpp_0706.reference_description: Write a function to find whether an array is subset of another array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find whether an array is subset of another array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Title: Subset check of two integer arrays. Main goal: Determine whether the second array (up to length n2) is a subset of the first array (up to length n). How: It builds a HashSet of the first n elements of nArray, then iterates through the first n2 elements of nArray2 and returns false if any element is not contained in the set; returns true if all are contained. Notes: uses helper methods I and l that implement n < n2 and n == 0, respectively, with some decompiled-appearance quirks.

mbpp_0874.reference_description: Write a java function to check if the string is a concatenation of another string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check if the string is a concatenation of another string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: ConcatChecker.checkConcat
Main goal: Determine whether the first input string is exactly formed by repeating (concatenating) the second input string one or more times. The method returns true only if string.length is a multiple of string2.length and every character at position i in string equals the corresponding character in string2 at position i % string2.length; otherwise it returns false. (Note: if string2 is empty, the code would encounter a division by zero in the modulo operation.)

mbpp_0026.reference_description: Write a function to check if the given tuple array has all k elements.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if the given tuple array has all k elements.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: All-elements-equal-to-n validator (2D list)

Main goal: The function checkKElements(List<List<Integer>> list, int n) returns true only if every integer in every inner list equals the given value n; otherwise it returns false. It iterates all elements, flags any mismatch, and finally returns the flag. It uses small helpers I and l, and contains obfuscated no-op code likely from decompilation.

mbpp_0969.reference_description: Write a function to join the tuples if they have similar initial elements.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to join the tuples if they have similar initial elements.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Summary_description
Title: TupleJoiner - Merging consecutive tuples with identical first element

Main goal: The joinTuples method processes a list of lists (tuples) and produces a new list of lists where consecutive tuples that share the same first element are merged by concatenating their tails (elements from index 1 onward) into the last accumulated list. If the next tuple has a different first element, a new inner list is started. In short, it groups adjacent rows by their leading element and appends their remaining elements into a single list per group.

mbpp_0952.reference_description: Write a function to compute the value of ncr mod p.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to compute the value of ncr mod p.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Computes C(n, r) modulo p by iteratively building a small DP array (Pascal's triangle style), using r = min(r, n-r) for efficiency, and returning the result modulo p.

mbpp_0025.reference_description: Write a java function to find the product of non-repeated elements in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the product of non-repeated elements in a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Product of distinct values in a sorted array (quirky all-equal handling)

Main goal: The code sorts the input array and then computes a product by multiplying certain elements that demarcate changes in value. Specifically, it multiplies an array element whenever its value differs from the previous element (with the first element compared to the last for wrap-around). Effectively, it returns the product of the distinct values present in the array; however, if all elements are the same, it returns 1. Helper methods implement the loop boundary (I), the zero-index check (l), and the not-equal check (Il).

mbpp_0125.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum difference between the number of 0s and number of 1s in any sub-string of the given binary string.

Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Kadane-like maximum subarray on zero-vs-nonzero characters
Main goal: Iterate through the first n characters of the input string, treating '0' as +1 and every other character as -1, and return the maximum subarray sum found (i.e., the maximum score of a contiguous substring), resetting the running sum to 0 when it becomes negative. Helper methods implement basic equality, less-than, and negativity checks (as used by the obfuscated decompiled code).

mbpp_0101.reference_description: Write a function to find the kth element in the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the kth element in the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: KthElementFinder - bubble-sort-based kth smallest element retrieval

Main goal: Compute the k-th smallest element in the first n elements of an integer array by performing a bubble-sort-like process and returning the element at index k-1 after sorting.

Summary of the functions:
- kthElement(int[] nArray, int n, int n2): Repeatedly performs bubble-sort passes on the first n elements of the array. After these passes, it returns the element at position n2 - 1, i.e., the k-th smallest value (1-based k) among the first n elements. The inner loop swaps adjacent elements when the left one is larger than the right one, effectively bubbling the largest element to the end of the current unsorted portion. The outer loop repeats this for n passes to fully sort the first n elements.
- I(int n, int n2): returns true if n < n2.
- l(int n, int n2): returns true if n > n2.

Notes:
- There are obfuscated/decompiler artifacts (e.g., useless "" .length() calls and always-true continue statements) that do not affect the core logic; they are effectively no-ops.

mbpp_0142.reference_description: Write a function to count the same pair in three given arrays.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to count the same pair in three given arrays.

mbpp_0111.reference_description: Write a function to find common elements in given nested arrays. * array item * array item * array item * array item

It initializes a set with the first inner list and iteratively intersects it with each subsequent inner list (retainAll). If the outer list is null or empty, it returns an empty list. Note: it uses raw types and contains decompiler artifacts that are effectively no-ops.

mbpp_0147.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum total path sum in the given triangle.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum total path sum in the given triangle.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Response:
Title: Triangle Maximum Path Sum (in-place, bottom-up DP)

Main goal: Given a triangular 2D int array (row i has i+1 elements), the code computes the maximum possible sum from the top to the bottom by propagating the larger of the two possible downward moves (left-down or right-down) from each cell, processing from the bottom row up. mbpp_0187.reference_description: Write a function to find the longest common subsequence for the given two sequences.

mbpp_0343.reference_description: Write a function to calculate the number of digits and letters in a string.

Goal: Given a string, count how many alphabetic characters and how many digits it contains, and return those counts as an int array [letters, digits].

mbpp_0385.reference_description: Write a function to find the n'th perrin number using recursion.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the n'th perrin number using recursion.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Perrin sequence calculator (recursive)
Main goal: Implement a recursive function getPerrin(n) that returns the Perrin number P(n) with base cases P(0)=3, P(1)=0, P(2)=2 and recurrence P(n)=P(n-2)+P(n-3) for n>2. It uses helper methods:

mbpp_0831.reference_description: Write a java function to count equal element pairs from the given array.

mbpp_0867.reference_description: Write a java function to add a minimum number such that the sum of array becomes even.

mbpp_0403.reference_description: Write a function to check if a url is valid or not using regex.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if a url is valid or not using regex.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Goal: Provide a simple URL detector that checks whether a given string contains a substring matching a specific HTTP/HTTPS URL pattern. mbpp_0635.reference_description: Write a function to push all values into a heap and then pop off the smallest values one at a time.

mbpp_0949.reference_description: Write a function to sort the given tuple array basis the total digits in tuple.

mbpp_0095.reference_description: Write a java function to find the minimum length of sublist.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the minimum length of sublist.

mbpp_0093.reference_description: Write a function to calculate the value of 'a' to the power 'b'.

mbpp_0166.reference_description: Write a java function to count the pairs with xor as an even number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count the pairs with xor as an even number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Count pairs of array elements with the same parity
Main goal: Given an int array and its length, the code computes how many pairs (i, j) with i < j have elements that share the same parity (both even or both odd). It uses a brute-force double loop to examine every pair and increments the counter when (a[i] ^ a[j]) % 2 == 0, which is equivalent to a[i] and a[j] having the same least-significant bit. Helper methods implement simple comparisons used in the condition.

mbpp_0167.reference_description: Write a java function to find smallest power of 2 greater than or equal to n.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find smallest power of 2 greater than or equal to n.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: NextPowerOf2 — Compute the next power of two for a given integer

Main goal: Given an int n, return the smallest power of two that is greater than or equal to n. If n is already a power of two, it returns n; if n is 0 it returns 1. The code uses helpers I(n) (n != 0) and l(n) (n == 0). Note: there is decompiler noise in the loop, and negative inputs are not safely handled (they could hang).

mbpp_0241.reference_description: Write a function to generate a 3d array having each element as '*'.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to generate a 3d array having each element as '*'.

Title: Array3DGenerator

mbpp_0127.reference_description: Write a function to multiply two integers without using the * operator in java.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to multiply two integers without using the * operator in java.

It handles negative multipliers by negating the recursive result, returns 0 when the multiplier is 0, and returns n when the multiplier is 1. It uses helper methods I (checks if n < 0), l (checks if n == 0), and Il (checks if n == m) for base cases. Potential issues include integer overflow and a problematic edge case for Integer.MIN_VALUE, which can cause infinite recursion due to negation overflow.

mbpp_0556.reference_description: Write a java function to count the pairs with xor as an odd number.

Description_Simple.comparison_text:

mbpp_0527.reference_description: Write a function to find all pairs in an integer array whose sum is equal to a given number.

mbpp_0564.reference_description: Write a java function to count unequal element pairs from the given array.

mbpp_0841.reference_description: Write a function to count the number of inversions in the given array.

mbpp_0767.reference_description: Write a java function to count the number of pairs whose sum is equal to ‘sum’.

It uses a nested i < j loop to examine all pairs and increments a counter when a[i] + a[j] == n2; includes tiny helper methods for equality (l) and less-than (I). mbpp_0849.reference_description: Write a java function to find sum of all prime divisors of a given number.

mbpp_0611.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum of nth column from the given tuple array.

mbpp_0914.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the given string is made up of two alternating characters or not.

mbpp_0103.reference_description: Write a function to find eulerian number a(n, m).

- A(n, m) = 0 if m >= n or n <= 0

mbpp_0165.reference_description: Write a java function to count characters at same position in a given string (lower and uppercase characters) as in english alphabet.

mbpp_0291.reference_description: Write a function to find out the number of ways of painting the fence such that at most 2 adjacent posts have the same color for the given fence with n posts and k colors.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find out the number of ways of painting the fence such that at most 2 adjacent posts have the same color for the given fence with n posts and k colors.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Goal: compute the number of ways to color n fence posts with n2 colors (mod 1e9+7) using a dynamic programming approach. It defines dp[1] = n2 (if n >= 1) and dp[2] = n2^2 (if n >= 2), then for i from 3 to n uses the recurrence dp[i] = (n2 - 1) * (dp[i-1] + dp[i-2]) mod 1e9+7. The result returned is dp[n]. This matches the classic paint-fence DP pattern (dp[i] = (k-1)(dp[i-1] + dp[i-2])) with k colors, though the base case for dp[2] appears incorrect for the standard problem (it should be k*(k-1)). The code also contains decompiler artifacts (unneeded string length calls and a condition that always continues).

mbpp_0562.reference_description: Write a java function to find the maximum length of sublist.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the maximum length of sublist.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code defines MaxLengthFinder.findMaxLength, which takes a List of List<?> and returns the maximum inner list size found. It iterates over each inner list, updating the current maximum length when it encounters a longer inner list. Some extra no-op lines are present (obfuscated) that do not affect the result.

mbpp_0461.reference_description: Write a java function to count the upper case characters in a given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count the upper case characters in a given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: UpperCounter - Checks if the first character is an uppercase Latin letter

Main goal: The method upperCtr(String) returns 1 if the input string is non-empty and its first character is between 'A' (65) and 'Z' (90) in ASCII; otherwise it returns 0. It uses small helper methods to perform simple range checks (n >= m, n < m, n <= m) on the first character's code.

mbpp_0683.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the given number can be represented by sum of two squares or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the given number can be represented by sum of two squares or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: SumSquareChecker
Main goal: Check if n can be written as the sum of squares of two positive integers (n = a^2 + b^2, a,b ≥ 1) using a brute-force double loop.

mbpp_0352.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether all the characters in a given string are unique.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether all the characters in a given string are unique.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: UniqueCharacters - String Uniqueness Checker
Main goal: Determine if a given string contains only unique characters by comparing every pair of characters; returns true if all characters are distinct and false if any duplicate exists. The code uses a naive O(n^2) approach with helper methods l (equality) and I (less-than).

mbpp_0764.reference_description: Write a java function to count numeric values in a given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count numeric values in a given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code defines a NumberCounter class with a method numberCtr(String) that counts how many characters in the input string are digits ('0' to '9', ASCII codes 48–57) and returns that count. It uses small helper methods to implement simple range checks (>=, <, <=) for the character codes. Some decompiler-generated artifacts appear in the loop but do not affect the overall digit-counting behavior.

mbpp_0818.reference_description: Write a java function to count lower case letters in a given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count lower case letters in a given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: LowerCounter – Counts lowercase ASCII letters in a string

Main goal: The code defines a class LowerCounter with a method lowerCtr that iterates through a given string and returns the count of characters whose ASCII codes lie between 97 and 122 (i.e., 'a' through 'z'). It uses small helper methods for range comparisons (l: >=, I: <, Il: <=). There are some decompiler artifacts (no-op lines) that do not affect the final result.

mbpp_0803.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the given number is a perfect square or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the given number is a perfect square or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: PerfectSquareChecker - detects perfect squares

Main goal: Determine whether a given integer n is a perfect square. The code iterates potential square roots n2 starting from 1 while n2^2 <= n, and for each n2 checks if n is divisible by n2 and if n/n2 equals n2. If such a pair is found, it returns true; otherwise it returns false. Helper methods Il, I, and l implement simple comparisons used in the checks. Note: 0 is not considered a perfect square by this implementation, and there are decompiler artifacts that act as no-ops.

mbpp_0028.reference_description: Write a java function to find binomial co-efficient.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find binomial co-efficient.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: BinomialCoefficient Calculator

Main goal: Compute the binomial coefficient C(n, k) using a simple recursive implementation of Pascal's rule.

What it does:
- binomialCoeff(int n, int n2): Returns C(n, n2). Handles base cases and recursion.
  - If n2 > n (k > n): returns 0.
  - If n2 == 0 or n2 == n (k == 0 or k == n): returns 1.
  - Otherwise: returns binomialCoeff(n-1, n2-1) + binomialCoeff(n-1, n2) (Pascal's rule).

Helper methods (obfuscated names, same semantics):
- Il(int n, int n2): true if n == n2 (k == n).
- I(int n, int n2): true if n > n2 (k > n).
- l(int n): true if n != 0 (k != 0).

Overall, the class computes the standard binomial coefficient using a recursive approach with the usual base cases.

mbpp_0346.reference_description: Write a function to find entringer number e(n, k).

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find entringer number e(n, k).
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Zigzag zeta-like two-parameter recursion
Main goal: Compute an integer via a naive two-argument recurrence. Base cases: if both n and n2 are 0, return 1; if only n2 is 0, return 0. Otherwise return zigzag(n, n2-1) + zigzag(n-1, n-n2). The helper I(n) simply checks whether a value is 0. The function effectively counts/combines subproblems in a way reminiscent of lattice-path or combinatorial counts, but with an exponential time complexity due to overlapping subproblems and no memoization.

mbpp_0150.reference_description: Write a java function to find whether the given number is present in the infinite sequence or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find whether the given number is present in the infinite sequence or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: SequenceUtils doesContainB - membership in an arithmetic progression
Main goal: Determine whether n2 is part of the arithmetic progression that starts at n and increases by n3 each step, including the starting value. The method returns true if n2 == n, or if (n2 - n) is a positive multiple of n3 (i.e., n2 = n + k*n3 for some k > 0). The helper methods perform basic checks: l compares equality, ll checks for zero, Il checks for positive, and I is a three-way long comparator (-1, 0, 1). Note: if n3 == 0 and n2 != n, the result is false due to short-circuit evaluation.

mbpp_0464.reference_description: Write a function to check if all values are same in map.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if all values are same in map.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: A generic utility method that checks if a map contains a given value. It iterates over the map’s values and returns true if any value equals the provided value v, with special handling for null (if v is null, it returns true only if a null value exists in the map; otherwise it looks for an equal non-null value).

mbpp_0126.reference_description: Write a java function to find the sum of common divisors of two given numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the sum of common divisors of two given numbers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: CommonDivisorsSum – sum of common divisors below the smaller input

Main goal: Given two integers n and n2, compute the sum of all positive integers d such that:
- d < min(n, n2), and
- d divides both n and n2 (i.e., n % d == 0 and n2 % d == 0).

The result is returned as the accumulator sum. The code uses helper methods: I checks the loop bound (n < min(n, n2)) and l checks divisibility (n == 0 after modulo). The function also contains obfuscated, dead code that has no effect on the result (unreachable return and always-true conditional).

mbpp_0923.reference_description: Write a function to find the length of the shortest string that has both str1 and str2 as subsequences.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the length of the shortest string that has both str1 and str2 as subsequences.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Shortest Common Supersequence Length Calculator
Main goal: Compute the length of the shortest common supersequence (SCS) of two strings using a recursive approach. Given two strings and their lengths n and n2, it:
- returns n2 if n == 0, or n if n2 == 0 (base cases),
- if the last characters match, returns 1 + SCS(string, string2, n-1, n2-1),
- otherwise returns 1 + min(SCS(string, string2, n-1, n2), SCS(string, string2, n, n2-1)).

mbpp_0891.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the given two numbers have same number of digits or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the given two numbers have same number of digits or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: SameLength - check if two integers have the same number of digits
Main goal: Determine whether two integers have the same decimal digit length.
Notes: The method repeatedly divides both numbers by 10 while both are positive, then returns true if both become zero (otherwise false). It treats positive numbers and the special case of both zeros as having the same length, but returns false for negative inputs or when one is zero and the other is not. The code contains obfuscated, dead/unreachable statements from decompilation.

mbpp_0334.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the triangle is valid or not if sides are given.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the triangle is valid or not if sides are given.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: TriangleValidator - triangle-inequality validator
Main goal: Check if three numbers can form the sides of a triangle by enforcing the triangle inequalities: d + d2 > d3, d + d3 > d2, and d2 + d3 > d. It uses small helper methods to compare sums and interpret the signs.

mbpp_0521.reference_description: Write a function to print check if the triangle is scalene or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to print check if the triangle is scalene or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Scalene side check (pairwise distinct lengths)
Main goal: Determine if three given integers represent a scalene configuration by ensuring all three pairwise comparisons are unequal. Note: it does not verify triangle inequality, so it only checks distinctness of sides, not validity as a triangle.

mbpp_0630.reference_description: Write a function to extract all the adjacent coordinates of the given coordinate tuple.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to extract all the adjacent coordinates of the given coordinate tuple.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: AdjacentCoordinates – enumerate adjacent-value coordinate combinations

Main goal: Given an int[] nArray, produce all lists of integers of the same length where every element is within ±1 of the corresponding input value (i.e., values in [nArray[i]-1, nArray[i], nArray[i]+1]). The method getCoordinates returns all such combinations as a List<List<Integer>>.

How it works: It uses a recursive helper generate starting at index 0. For each position i, it iterates n2 from nArray[i]-1 up to nArray[i]+1 (inclusive), appends n2 to a running path, recurses to the next index, and then backtracks. When the end of the array is reached, it stores a copy of the current path.

Notes: The I and l methods implement equality and a bound check (n == n2 and n <= n2, respectively). The extra string-length checks are artifacts of decompilation and have no effect.

mbpp_0255.reference_description: Write a function to choose specified number of colours from three different colours and generate all the combinations with repetitions.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to choose specified number of colours from three different colours and generate all the combinations with repetitions.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: ColorCombinations – Backtracking to generate combinations with repetition
Main goal: Given a list of strings and an integer n, generate all length-n combinations where elements are chosen from the list with repetition allowed (i.e., non-decreasing index selections). The public method combinationsColors(list, n) starts the process, and the private backtrack(...) builds current combinations and collects all results. Helper methods I and l perform simple equality and less-than checks. The code appears decompiled and includes some non-functional artifacts, but the core logic is standard backtracking to enumerate combinations with repetition.

mbpp_0462.reference_description: Write a function to find all possible combinations of the elements of a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find all possible combinations of the elements of a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Combinations - Subset (power set) generator
Main goal: Given a list, generate all possible subsets (combinations) of its elements, including the empty subset, by recursively computing combinations of the tail and then combining each with and without the head.

mbpp_0148.reference_description: Write a function to divide a number into two parts such that the sum of digits is maximum.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to divide a number into two parts such that the sum of digits is maximum.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Digit-Sum Decomposition Utilities
Main goal: Provide methods to sum digits of a nonnegative long (sumDigitsSingle), find the largest all-9s number not exceeding a given value (closest), and compute the maximal possible sum of digits when splitting a number into two nonnegative addends by using the all-9s component (sumDigitsTwoParts). Private helpers implement simple sign/comparison logic used to drive the loops.

mbpp_0540.reference_description: Write a java function to find the difference between highest and least frequencies in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the difference between highest and least frequencies in a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Difference of run-length adjacencies in a sorted array

Main goal: Given an integer array nArray and an integer n, sort the array and, for each group of identical consecutive values, count the number of adjacent equal pairs (which is run_length - 1). Track the maximum and minimum such counts across all groups and return their difference (max - min). The code uses helper methods l for equality and I for less-than. Note: a bug causes the last run to be ignored, potentially yielding incorrect results when the array ends with a uniform run.

mbpp_0259.reference_description: Write a function to maximize the given two tuples.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to maximize the given two tuples.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Element-wise maximum of two 2D integer lists

Main goal: Given two List<List<Integer>> inputs, produce a new List<List<Integer>> where, for each corresponding pair of inner lists (up to the shorter outer size), each element is the maximum of the two input elements at that position (up to the shorter inner size).

mbpp_0348.reference_description: Write a function to count sequences of given length having non-negative prefix sums that can be generated by given values.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to count sequences of given length having non-negative prefix sums that can be generated by given values.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: SequenceCounter — binomial and Catalan computations
Main goal: Provide utilities to compute binomial coefficients and Catalan numbers. 
- binCoff(n, k) calculates the binomial coefficient C(n, k) using a multiplicative recurrence and symmetry optimization (uses min(k, n-k)).
- findWays(n) returns the Catalan number for floor(n/2) by computing Catalan(m) = C(2m, m) / (m+1) with m = floor(n/2).
- l and I are simple comparison helpers used by the calculations.

mbpp_0445.reference_description: Write a function to perform index wise multiplication of tuple elements in the given two tuples.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to perform index wise multiplication of tuple elements in the given two tuples.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Element-wise multiplication of corresponding elements in two lists of lists
Main goal: Given two lists of lists of integers, produce a new list of lists where each inner list contains the products of corresponding elements from the two input inner lists. The operation respects the shorter extent of both outer lists and, for each pair of inner lists, the shorter inner length, effectively performing a min-length, pairwise multiplication across matching indices.

mbpp_0598.reference_description: Write a function to check whether the given number is armstrong or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check whether the given number is armstrong or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: ArmstrongNumberChecker: A Java utility that tests whether a given integer n is an Armstrong (narcissistic) number by counting its digits and verifying that n equals the sum of its digits each raised to the power of the digit count. It uses a static isArmstrong method plus helpers l (equality) and I (positive check); note: the decompiled code contains no-op lines that do not affect logic.

mbpp_0844.reference_description: Write a java function to find the kth element in an array containing odd elements first and then even elements.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the kth element in an array containing odd elements first and then even elements.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Odd-First Sequence Element Retriever
Main goal: Build a list of integers from 1 to n with all odd numbers first (ascending), followed by all even numbers (ascending), and return the element at position n2 (1-based) in that list.

mbpp_0289.reference_description: Write a java function to calculate the number of odd days in a given year.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to calculate the number of odd days in a given year.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: OddDaysCalculator - compute odd days after n years
Main goal: Return the number of odd days (days modulo 7) accumulated in the first n years under the Gregorian calendar by counting leap years and ordinary years and applying century/400-year rules. The oddDays(n) method performs the calculation; I(int) is a helper that checks non-zero.

mbpp_0631.reference_description: Write a function to replace whitespaces with an underscore and vice versa in a given string by using regex.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to replace whitespaces with an underscore and vice versa in a given string by using regex.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Swap spaces and underscores in a string
Main goal: The replaceSpaces method takes a string and swaps every space with an underscore and every underscore with a space, returning the transformed string. It uses a regex pattern "[ _]" with a Matcher to perform per-match replacements.

mbpp_0005.reference_description: Write a function to find the number of ways to fill it with 2 x 1 dominoes for the given 3 x n board.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the number of ways to fill it with 2 x 1 dominoes for the given 3 x n board.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Summary_description
- Title: Dynamic programming tiling of 2×n board with dominoes and L-trominoes
- Main goal: Compute the number of ways to tile a 2×n board using 2×1 dominoes and L-shaped trominoes by a DP with two sequences A[n] (lArray) and B[n] (lArray2). The recurrences are A[n] = A[n-2] + 2*B[n-1] and B[n] = A[n-1] + B[n-2], with base cases A[0]=1, A[1]=0, B[0]=0, B[1]=1. The function returns A[n].

mbpp_0045.reference_description: Write a function to find the gcd of the given array elements.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the gcd of the given array elements.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: GCDUtil - Euclidean GCD Calculator
Main goal: Compute the greatest common divisor of two integers (findGcd) and of an array of integers (getGcd) using the Euclidean algorithm; the code includes obfuscated no-op statements.

mbpp_0645.reference_description: Write a function to find the product of it’s kth index in the given tuples.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the product of it’s kth index in the given tuples.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Product Calculator for Integer Lists
Main goal: Provide two utilities: getProduct computes the product of all integers in a single List<Integer> (returns 1 for an empty list), and findKProduct takes a List<List<Integer>> and an index n, collects the nth element from each inner list into a new list, and returns the product of those elements by calling getProduct. The I method is a small decompiler artifact used to drive while loops, and many no-op statements are present but do not affect the logic.

mbpp_0709.reference_description: Write a function to count unique keys for each value present in the tuple.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to count unique keys for each value present in the tuple.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Count of Unique Keys per Value
Main goal: The getUnique method takes a list of key-value pairs (AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<K,V>) and returns a map from each value V to the number of distinct keys K that map to that value. It builds a V -> Set<K> mapping to deduplicate keys, then converts that to a V -> Integer mapping representing the size of each key set. The code includes decompiler artefacts and obfuscated checks, but the core logic is counting how many unique keys correspond to each value.

mbpp_0164.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the sum of divisors are same or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the sum of divisors are same or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: DivisorUtils - Divisor sum calculator and equivalence checker
Main goal: Provide a divisor sum function (divSum) and a comparison function (areEquivalent) to test whether two integers have the same sum of divisors. Note: divSum has a flaw (it double-counts the square-root divisor for perfect squares and omits the number itself in the sum).
