Title: RemoveOdd method extracts even-position characters
Main goal: Given a string, build and return a new string consisting of characters at even positions (2nd, 4th, 6th, ... in 1-based indexing), effectively removing the odd-positioned characters.

mbpp_0436.reference_description: Write a java function to print negative numbers in array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to print negative numbers in array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Title: First negative number finder. Main goal: Return the first negative Integer in the given List<Integer>; if none exist, return null. The extra no-op lines and decompiler artifacts don't affect the logic.

mbpp_0443.reference_description: Write a java function to find the largest negative number from the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the largest negative number from the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Find the minimum element in an int array
Main goal: The method largestNeg returns the smallest value present in the input int[] by iterating through all elements and updating a running minimum. It uses a helper I(int a, int b) that returns a < b. There is dead/obfuscated code sprinkled in that does not affect the outcome.

mbpp_0633.reference_description: Write a java function to find the sum of xor of all pairs of numbers in the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the sum of xor of all pairs of numbers in the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Pairwise XOR Sum
Main goal: Compute the sum of bitwise XORs over all distinct pairs (i, j) with 0 ≤ i < j < n in the given integer array.

mbpp_0666.reference_description: Write a function to count occurrence of a character in a string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to count occurrence of a character in a string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Counts occurrences of a given character in a string. The countChar method iterates through the string, compares each character to the target using a small helper, and increments a counter when they match; it returns the number of times the character appears. The class also contains tiny helper methods for equality and less-than checks, plus obfuscated/no-op code that doesn’t affect the actual counting.

mbpp_0610.reference_description: Write a java function to remove the k'th element from a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to remove the k'th element from a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Remove kth element from a list
Main goal: Return a new list that is a copy of the input, with the kth element (1-based) removed when k is within bounds; if k is out of bounds, return the copy unchanged. The method preserves the original list and performs a 0-based removal at index k-1 when valid.

mbpp_0567.reference_description: Write a function to check whether a specified array is sorted or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check whether a specified array is sorted or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: SortUtils.isSortedList
Goal: Determine whether a List<T> (where T extends Comparable) is sorted in ascending order by comparing each adjacent pair; returns false if any pair is out of order, true otherwise. The extra no-op lines are artifacts of decompilation; the core logic is a simple adjacent comparison loop.

mbpp_0695.reference_description: Write a function to check if each element of the second tuple is greater than its corresponding index in the first tuple.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if each element of the second tuple is greater than its corresponding index in the first tuple.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Element-wise strict less-than check between two int arrays
Main goal: The checkGreater method returns true if, for every index i up to the shorter of the two array lengths, nArray[i] is strictly less than nArray2[i]. It returns false if it finds any position where nArray[i] >= nArray2[i]. If there is no overlapping index (one array is empty), it returns true. The private helpers implement >= and < comparisons, and there are obfuscated no-op statements from decompilation.

mbpp_0741.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether all the characters are same or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether all the characters are same or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: AllCharactersSame
Main goal: Determine whether all characters in a provided string are the same. The method iterates through the string (starting from index 1) and returns false if any character differs from the first character; it returns true for empty strings or strings of length 1 as well as when every character matches the first. It uses simple helper methods I(n, m) -> n < m and l(a, b) -> a != b, and contains decompiler-added no-op code.

mbpp_0667.reference_description: Write a java function to count number of vowels in the string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count number of vowels in the string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: VowelCounter — Counts matching characters from one string in another

Main goal: Given two strings, CheckVow returns the number of characters in the first string that are also present in the second string (i.e., counts how many characters of string1 appear in string2; if string2 lists vowels, it effectively counts vowels in string1). The helper methods are simple boolean/comparison utilities, and the extra no-op lines are artifacts from decompilation.

mbpp_0807.reference_description: Write a java function to find the first odd number in a given array of numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the first odd number in a given array of numbers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: FirstOddFinder - Find first odd integer in a list
Main goal: Iterate over a List<Integer> and return the first odd number; if no odd exists, return -1.

mbpp_0897.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the word is present in a given sentence or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the word is present in a given sentence or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
WordChecker: Word presence checker in a sentence

Main goal:
- To determine whether a given word (string2) appears as one of the space-delimited tokens in another string (string).

Key behavior:
- isWordPresent(String string, String string2): splits string by spaces, iterates over the resulting tokens, and returns true if any token equals string2; otherwise returns false.
- I(int n, int n2): helper that simply checks if n < n2, used as the loop condition.
- l(int n): helper that converts an int to a boolean (true if nonzero); used to interpret the result of the equality check string3.equals(string2) as a boolean.
- The equality check is effectively string3.equals(string2); the surrounding helpers and extra decompiled artifacts (like redundant assignments and meaningless length tricks) do not change the actual logic.

mbpp_0809.reference_description: Write a function to check if each element of second tuple is smaller than its corresponding index in first tuple.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if each element of second tuple is smaller than its corresponding index in first tuple.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Checker.checkSmaller - element-wise greater-than comparison of two int arrays
Main goal: Return true if every pair of corresponding elements from the two input arrays (up to the length of the shorter array) satisfies nArray[i] > nArray2[i]; return false if any pair has nArray[i] <= nArray2[i]. It uses the minimum of the two lengths to bound the loop and two helper methods I and l implement the comparisons (< and <=). Note: there are some decompiler artifacts in the loop that are no-ops and do not affect the result.

mbpp_0942.reference_description: Write a function to check if any array element is present in the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if any array element is present in the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Common element existence in two lists
Main goal: Check if two List<T> objects have any element in common by iterating the second list and testing containment in the first; returns true on first match, otherwise false.

mbpp_0909.reference_description: Write a function to find the previous palindrome of a specified number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the previous palindrome of a specified number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: PreviousPalindrome
Main goal: Given a positive integer n, find and return the largest palindrome strictly less than n; if no such positive palindrome exists, return 0. It does this by decrementing from n-1 downward, testing each number by converting it to a string and checking if it reads the same forward and backward. The helper methods validate positivity/nonzero, and some decompiled no-op statements are present but do not affect the logic.

mbpp_0260.reference_description: Write a function to find the nth newman–shanks–williams prime number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the nth newman–shanks–williams prime number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Newman-Shanks-Williams sequence calculator
Main goal: Compute the nth term a(n) of the Newman–Shanks–Williams sequence using a0 = a1 = 1 and the recurrence a_n = 2*a_{n-1} + a_{n-2}. The method returns 1 for n = 0 or n = 1 and uses naive recursion to build larger terms as BigInteger values (no memoization). This code generates terms associated with the NS-W sequence, which are used in certain primality tests, but it does not perform primality testing itself.

mbpp_0675.reference_description: Write a function to add two integers. however, if the sum is between the given range it will return 20.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to add two integers. however, if the sum is between the given range it will return 20.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: It defines a small Java class with a method sumNums that adds the first two arguments (n + n2). It then checks if the sum is at least n3 and strictly less than n4 using two helper predicates: I(n, n2) returns true if n >= n2, and l(n, n2) returns true if n < n2. If both conditions hold, it returns 20; otherwise it returns the sum.

mbpp_0955.reference_description: Write a function to find out, if the given number is abundant.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find out, if the given number is abundant.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
AbundantChecker: Abundance detector

Main goal: Determine if a given integer n is abundant by summing all proper divisors (positive divisors less than n that divide n) and returning true if that sum exceeds n. It includes helper predicates I(n, n2) for n < n2, Il(n, n2) for n > n2, and l(n) for n == 0; the method also contains obfuscated no-op lines that do not affect the logic.

mbpp_0960.reference_description: Write a function to solve tiling problem.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to solve tiling problem.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: This class computes the nth Fibonacci number using naive recursion. It uses base cases for n = 0 and n = 1 (implemented by private methods I and l) and the recurrence getNoOfWays(n) = getNoOfWays(n-1) + getNoOfWays(n-2); the method name is misleading, as it returns Fibonacci values rather than tiling counts.

mbpp_0796.reference_description: Write function to find the sum of all items in the given map.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write function to find the sum of all items in the given map.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Code Title: Obfuscated Map Value Sum

Main goal: Compute the sum of all Integer values stored in the given Map.

Summary:
- The method returnSum(Map<?, Integer> map) iterates over the map’s values and accumulates their sum into n.
- It uses a helper I(int n) that returns true if n != 0 to drive the loop via the condition Solution.I(iterator.hasNext() ? 1 : 0).
- The body effectively adds each value to n; there are extra no-op lines (dead code) inserted to confuse decompilers, which do not affect the result.
- If the map is empty, it returns 0. Note: if any map value is null, it could throw a NullPointerException due to unboxing.

mbpp_0790.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether every even index contains even numbers of a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether every even index contains even numbers of a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Checks if every array element has the same parity as its index (0-based): even indices must contain even numbers and odd indices must contain odd numbers. It iterates through the array and returns false if any element’s parity differs from its index parity; otherwise, it returns true. Some extra dead code appears due to decompilation.

mbpp_0775.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether every odd index contains odd numbers of a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether every odd index contains odd numbers of a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Parity-alignment checker for array elements
Main goal: Determine whether every element in the input int array has the same parity as its index (even indices hold even numbers, odd indices hold odd numbers). Returns true if all elements match this pattern; false if any mismatch is found. Note: some decompiler artifacts (useless length() calls) are present but do not affect the logic.

mbpp_0713.reference_description: Write a function to check if the given tuple contains all valid values or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if the given tuple contains all valid values or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: This code defines a Main class with a method checkValid(boolean[]) that iterates over the input boolean array and returns true only if all elements are true; if any element is false, it returns false. It uses two helper methods: I(n, m) checks n < m to drive the loop, and l(x) checks x == 0 (used to detect a false value). There is additional decompiler noise (dead code) present that does not affect the logic.

mbpp_0802.reference_description: Write a java function to count the number of rotations required to generate a sorted array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count the number of rotations required to generate a sorted array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: RotationCounter - Pivot index finder in a rotated sorted array
Main goal: Given an integer array that is a rotated version of a non-decreasing sequence and its length n, determine the index where the rotation occurs. It returns the first index i (starting from 1) where a[i] < a[i-1]; if no such index exists, it returns 0.
How it works:
- countRotation(int[] nArray, int n): iterates i from 1 to n-1; if nArray[i] < nArray[i-1], it returns i. If no such i is found, it returns 0.
- I(int n, int n2): helper that returns n < n2.
Notes: There are decompiler artifacts (no-op lines) that do not affect the logic.

mbpp_0808.reference_description: Write a function to check if the given tuples contain the k or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if the given tuples contain the k or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: CheckK.checkK - Generic containment check in an array
Main goal: Implement a generic static method checkK(T[] TArray, T t) that returns true if the array contains an element equal to t (using equals), by iterating through the array with a while loop. It uses small helper methods I and l to perform the basic boolean checks, and contains some no-op lines that do not affect the outcome.

mbpp_0833.reference_description: Write a function to get map keys as array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to get map keys as array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Gather map keys into a list
Main goal: Return a List<K> containing all keys from the given Map<K, ?> by iterating over the map's keySet.

mbpp_0804.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the product of numbers is even or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the product of numbers is even or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Product Even Detector
Main goal: Determine whether the product of the first n elements of the given int array is even by returning true if any of the first n elements is even; otherwise false. The code iterates over the first n elements, checks parity via bitwise & 1 (even if result is 0), and returns true upon finding an even number; if none are even, it returns false. The helpers are simple bound-check and parity-check wrappers, and there is some obfuscated no-op code.

mbpp_0908.reference_description: Write a function to find the fixed point in the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the fixed point in the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Fixed Point Finder
Main goal: Find the first index i (0 <= i < n) such that array[i] == i in the given int array, returning i or -1 if no such fixed point exists within the first n elements. The helper methods check for n < n2 and n == n2, respectively. There is dead/obfuscated code present that does not affect the logic.

mbpp_0084.reference_description: Write a function to find the n-th number in newman conway sequence.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the n-th number in newman conway sequence.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: NewmanConway sequence calculator (recursive implementation)
Main goal: Implement the Newman-Conway sequence where S(1)=S(2)=1 and, for n>2, S(n)=S(S(n−1)) + S(n−S(n−1)). The code uses helper methods to define base cases and computes the value recursively (without memoization, leading to exponential time).

mbpp_0890.reference_description: Write a java function to find the index of an extra element present in one sorted array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the index of an extra element present in one sorted array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: ExtraElementFinder.findExtra - First mismatch index between two int arrays
Main goal: Return the smallest index i (0 <= i < n) where nArray[i] != nArray2[i]; if all first n elements match, return n.
Notes: Uses helpers I (checks i < n) and l (checks values are not equal); contains decompiler noise that does not affect logic.

mbpp_0889.reference_description: Write a function to reverse each array in a given array of arrays.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to reverse each array in a given array of arrays.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Reverse-sorting inner lists in a list of lists
Main goal: Given a List<List<T>> where T extends Comparable, iterate over each inner list and sort it in descending order in place, returning the original outer list. (Note: contains decompilation artifacts such as a useless String.length() call and an always-true conditional that create dead code.)

mbpp_0873.reference_description: Write a function to solve the fibonacci sequence using recursion.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to solve the fibonacci sequence using recursion.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Recursive Fibonacci Calculator
Main goal: Compute the nth Fibonacci number using a simple recursion F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2) with base cases F(1) = F(2) = 1. The code uses two tiny helpers: I(n, n2) checks inequality (n != n2) and l(n, n2) checks equality (n == n2); the base-case condition (!I(n,1) || l(n,2)) is equivalent to (n == 1 || n == 2). Note: there is no handling for n <= 0, which can lead to infinite recursion.

mbpp_0934.reference_description: Write a function to find the nth delannoy number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the nth delannoy number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Delannoy Numbers Calculator (naive recursive)
Goal: Compute Delannoy numbers D(m,n) using the standard recurrence D(m,n) = D(m-1,n) + D(m-1,n-1) + D(m,n-1) with base cases D(0,n) = 1 and D(m,0) = 1. The method dealnnoyNum(n, n2) effectively computes D(n2, n) by recursively summing D(n2-1, n), D(n2-1, n-1), and D(n2, n-1). Private helpers I and l implement the base-case checks. This is a straightforward, exponential-time recursive implementation without memoization.

mbpp_0198.reference_description: Write a function to find the largest triangle that can be inscribed in an ellipse.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the largest triangle that can be inscribed in an ellipse.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
EllipseUtils largestTriangle: compute a triangle-related measure from two inputs, with input validation.

Main goal: For non-negative inputs d and d2, return 3*sqrt(3)*d^2/(4*d2); if either input is negative, return -1.0. The class also provides small helpers:
- I(double d, double d2): returns -1 if d<d2, 0 if equal, 1 if d>d2.
- l(int n): true if n >= 0.
- Il(int n): true if n < 0.

mbpp_0081.reference_description: Write a function to zip the two given tuples.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to zip the two given tuples.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
ZipTuples: Zips two lists into a list of pairs.
Main goal: Create a generic method zipTuples(list, list2) that returns a List of Pair<T, U>, where each element i from the first list is paired with the element at index i modulo the size of the second list (i.e., the second list is cycled if shorter). It defines an inner Pair class to hold the two related elements. Note: the code contains decompiler artifacts and assumes the second list is non-empty.

mbpp_0766.reference_description: Write a function to iterate over all pairs of consecutive items in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to iterate over all pairs of consecutive items in a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Response: Title: PairWise – Generate adjacent element pairs; Main goal: Convert a List<T> into a List<Pair<T, T>> where each pair contains two consecutive elements (list[i], list[i+1]); returns an empty list for lists with fewer than 2 elements (using an inner generic Pair<T, U> class).

mbpp_0061.reference_description: Write a java function to count number of substrings with the sum of digits equal to their length.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count number of substrings with the sum of digits equal to their length.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Count substrings with average digit 1
Main goal: Given a numeric string, count substrings where the sum of digits equals the substring length (average digit equals 1). It uses a prefix-sum difference approach: track prefixSum(i) - (i+1) values in a hashmap, accumulate counts of equal differences to total substrings, and return the result as a long.

mbpp_0391.reference_description: Write a function to convert more than one array to nested map.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to convert more than one array to nested map.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: A Converter class method that takes three parallel lists (K, V, W) and builds a list of single-entry maps, where each element is a map from K to another map (V -> W). It processes up to the smallest list size, pairing corresponding elements to produce List<Map<K, Map<V, W>>>. The extra no-op/inobvious code is just decompiler noise.

mbpp_0951.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum of similar indices in two arrays of tuples.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum of similar indices in two arrays of tuples.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Element-wise maximums from two lists of integer pairs
Main goal: Given two lists of Pair<Integer, Integer>, produce a new list by pairing corresponding elements up to the shorter list length, where each new Pair contains the maximum of the first components and the maximum of the second components from the corresponding input pairs.

mbpp_0545.reference_description: Write a java function to toggle only first and last bits of a given number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to toggle only first and last bits of a given number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: ToggleBits - Toggle the lowest and highest set bits of an integer
Main goal: Use bit-twiddling to construct a mask that has 1s at the least significant bit and at the most significant set bit of n, then XOR that mask with n to flip those two bits (with a special case returning 0 when n == 1).

mbpp_0669.reference_description: Write a function to check whether the given ip address is valid or not using regex.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check whether the given ip address is valid or not using regex.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code defines an IPValidator that uses a regex pattern to validate IPv4 addresses (four octets, each 0-255, separated by dots). The checkIP method returns "Valid IP address" for valid inputs and "Invalid IP address" for invalid ones. It also includes a redundant helper method that converts an integer to a boolean.

mbpp_0735.reference_description: Write a java function to toggle bits of the number except the first and the last bit.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to toggle bits of the number except the first and the last bit.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: BitToggler — Middle-Bits Toggler
Main goal: Provide a method toggleMiddleBits(int n) that flips a specific “middle” region of bits in n. The code computes a mask of those middle bits with setMiddleBits(n) and then returns n XOR mask. A special case short-circuits to return 1 when n == 1.

Details:
- I(int n, int n2) is a simple equality check and is used only to test if n equals 1.
- If n == 1, toggleMiddleBits returns 1.
- setMiddleBits(n) builds a mask by propagating the highest set bit of n downward (via successive shifts: >>1, >>2, >>4, >>8, >>16) and then computes (n>>1) ^ 1, effectively producing a mask that has 1s in bit positions 1 through (MSBIndex-1) and 0s elsewhere (with special handling for edge cases like n = 0 or n = 1).
- Consequently, toggleMiddleBits(n) returns n XOR mask, which flips the bits in the “middle” region (bits 1..p-1 where p is the index of the most significant 1 in n). For example, if n is a power of two with MSB at p, the mask is 2^p - 2 (bits 1..p-1 set), flipping those bits in n. If the mask is 0 (e.g., p = 1), n remains unchanged. For n = 0, the mask is 1, so the result is 1.

A private helper compares integers, used to check if the set size is 3.

mbpp_0905.reference_description: Write a java function to find the sum of squares of binomial co-efficients.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the sum of squares of binomial co-efficients.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: BinomialCoefficients - Central Binomial Coefficient Calculator

Main goal: Provide utilities to compute binomial-related numbers. The class defines:
- factorial(int n, int n2): computes the product n * (n+1) * ... * n2 (a range factorial). If n > n2, it returns 1.
- sumOfSquare(int n): computes the central binomial coefficient C(2n, n) by evaluating (n+1)(n+2)...(2n) divided by 1*2*...*n.
- I(int n, int n2): helper that returns true if n <= n2.

Notes: The method named factorial is not the standard factorial; it performs a rising product over a range. sumOfSquare uses this to obtain the central binomial coefficient, i.e., (2n)! / (n! n!). The code appears decompiled/obfuscated but implements the above functionality.

mbpp_0300.reference_description: Write a function to find the count of all binary sequences of length 2n such that sum of first n bits is same as sum of last n bits.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the count of all binary sequences of length 2n such that sum of first n bits is same as sum of last n bits.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:

The result is sum_{k=0}^n C(n,k)^2 = C(2n, n).

Functions:
- PATTERN: Precompiled regex "^[a-z]$|^([a-z]).*\\1$", matching either a single lowercase letter or a string that starts with a lowercase letter and ends with the same letter (via backreference to group 1).
- checkChar(String string): Creates a Matcher for the input and returns "Valid" if the input matches the pattern, otherwise "Invalid".
- I(int n): Helper that returns true if n is nonzero; used to convert the match result into a boolean condition.
Notes: The backreference \\1 ensures the last character matches the first when using the second alternative; the first alternative handles the single-letter case.

Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: SumDifference – Difference between the square of the sum and the sum of squares

Main goal: Given n, compute (1 + 2 + ... + n)^2 − (1^2 + 2^2 + ... + n^2). The method sums k and k^2 in a loop, then returns (sum of k)^2 − (sum of k^2); for n ≤ 0 it yields 0. The code effectively implements the known formula [n(n+1)/2]^2 − n(n+1)(2n+1)/6, with some obfuscated dead code present.

mbpp_0319.reference_description: Write a function to find all five characters long word in the given string by using regex.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find all five characters long word in the given string by using regex.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: StringUtil.findLongWord - collect five-letter words
Main goal: Return a list of all five-character word tokens found in the input string by applying the regex \b\w{5}\b and aggregating the matches. The method iterates through matcher.find() results, adds each matched word to a list, and returns that list. There is some extraneous, effectively dead code present in the decompiled version.

mbpp_0314.reference_description: Write a function to find out the maximum sum such that no two chosen numbers are adjacent for the given rectangular grid of dimension 2 x n.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find out the maximum sum such that no two chosen numbers are adjacent for the given rectangular grid of dimension 2 x n.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code defines a class with a method that, given a 2-row integer grid and a column count, attempts to compute the maximum sum obtainable by taking, for each column, the larger of the two row values and then summing over a contiguous range of columns. It treats the two rows as a sequence of per-column maxima and tries to find the best contiguous block (subarray) sum over those maxima. The function uses two running variables (n2 and n3) to track the current sum and the best sum so far, with a nonstandard update pattern. The I helper simply checks if the first integer is less than the second and is used to drive the loop. Note: the code contains decompiler artifacts (useless string-length lines) that don’t affect logic. The method assumes at least two rows in the input.

mbpp_0285.reference_description: Write a function that matches a string that has an a followed by two to three 'b'.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function that matches a string that has an a followed by two to three 'b'.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code defines a TextMatcher class with textMatchTwoThree(String) that checks whether the input contains the substring "abb" or "abbb" using the regex "ab{2,3}". It returns "Found a match!" when a match exists and "Not matched!" otherwise; it also includes a redundant I(int) helper that converts 0/1 to boolean.

mbpp_0539.reference_description: Write a function to create array containing the power of said number in bases raised to the corresponding number in the index using map function.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to create array containing the power of said number in bases raised to the corresponding number in the index using map function.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Element-wise exponentiation of two numeric lists: The code defines basesNumCorrespondingNum(list, list2) which returns a new list containing Math.pow(list.get(i), list2.get(i)) for i from 0 up to the shorter of the two input lists. It effectively computes base^exponent for corresponding elements and ignores any extra elements in the longer list. A small helper I(n, n2) checks the loop bound, and some no-op lines appear due to decompilation but do not affect the result.

mbpp_0656.reference_description: Write a java function to find the minimum sum of absolute differences of two arrays.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the minimum sum of absolute differences of two arrays.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code sorts two int arrays and computes the sum of the absolute differences between their corresponding elements for the first n positions (i.e., sum of |nArray[i] - nArray2[i]| for i = 0 to n-1). This implements the common approach to minimize the total difference by pairing sorted elements. The extra lines (like "".length() and if (null == null)) are no-ops from decompilation and do not affect the result.

mbpp_0444.reference_description: Write a function to trim each tuple by k in the given tuple array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to trim each tuple by k in the given tuple array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Takes a List of Lists and an integer n, builds a new list where each inner list is trimmed by removing the first n and last n elements (subList(n, size−n)), then returns the string representation of that new list. It uses an obfuscated boolean helper I(int) and contains some no-op/dead code; may throw runtime exceptions if inner lists are too short.

mbpp_0643.reference_description: Write a function that matches a word containing 'z', not at the start or end of the word.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function that matches a word containing 'z', not at the start or end of the word.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: TextMatcher - Non-boundary 'z' detector within words
Main goal: Determine if a given string contains a lowercase 'z' that is not at a word boundary (i.e., a 'z' inside a word) using the regex \Bz\B, and return a message indicating whether such a match exists.
How it works: textMatchWordzMiddle compiles the pattern \Bz\B, tests the input string with a Matcher, and returns "Found a match!" if a non-boundary 'z' is found; otherwise it returns "Not matched!". A helper method I(int n) converts the boolean result of finder to a boolean by interpreting 0 as false and non-zero as true. The I method simply checks n != 0.

mbpp_0794.reference_description: Write a function that matches a string that has an 'a' followed by anything, ending in 'b'.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function that matches a string that has an 'a' followed by anything, ending in 'b'.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: TextMatcher — Main goal: Determine if a given string contains a non-greedy substring that starts with the letter 'a' and ends with the letter 'b' at the end of the string (regex "a.*?b$"), returning "Found a match!" when found, or "Not matched!" otherwise. It includes a tiny helper I(int n) that converts the int result (1 or 0) to a boolean.

mbpp_0740.reference_description: Write a function to convert the given tuple to a key-value map using adjacent elements.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to convert the given tuple to a key-value map using adjacent elements.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: TupleConverter: List-to-Map converter
Main goal: Convert a flat List<Object> that stores alternating keys and values (e.g., [k1, v1, k2, v2, ...]) into a Map<Object, Object> by pairing consecutive elements as map entries (k at even indices with the following value). It uses a simple index check helper and includes no-op/decompiler artifacts; note that if the list length is odd, the code may throw an index error due to pairing beyond the end.

mbpp_0674.reference_description: Write a function to remove duplicate words from a given string using collections module.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to remove duplicate words from a given string using collections module.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Title: RemoveDuplicateWords. Main goal: Remove duplicate words from a string while preserving their original order by splitting on whitespace, collecting unique tokens in a LinkedHashSet, and joining them back with single spaces.

mbpp_0759.reference_description: Write a function to check a decimal with a precision of 2.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check a decimal with a precision of 2.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: DecimalUtils - decimal string validator
Main goal: Provide isDecimal(String) to check if input is a non-null numeric string consisting of digits with an optional decimal part having 1 or 2 digits, returning false for null or non-matching inputs.

mbpp_0944.reference_description: Write a function to separate and print the numbers and their position of a given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to separate and print the numbers and their position of a given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Start index of first numeric sequence
Main goal: Returns the starting index of the first run of digits in the input string, or null if there are no digits.

mbpp_0019.reference_description: Write a function to find whether a given array of integers contains any duplicate element.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find whether a given array of integers contains any duplicate element.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: DuplicateChecker - Duplicates detection in an int array
Main goal: Determine if a given int[] contains duplicate values. It builds a HashSet from all array elements and compares the original array length with the set size; if they differ, duplicates exist and the method returns true, otherwise it returns false. The code also includes two small helper methods that perform simple comparisons (likely artifacts of decompilation).

mbpp_0016.reference_description: Write a function to find sequences of lowercase letters joined with an underscore.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find sequences of lowercase letters joined with an underscore.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: TextUtils.textLowercaseUnderscore
Main goal: Validate whether an input string matches the pattern of two lowercase letter groups separated by a single underscore (regex "^[a-z]+_[a-z]+$") and return "Found a match!" if it does, otherwise "Not matched!". The I(int) helper is a redundant boolean converter used to obfuscate the condition.

mbpp_0956.reference_description: Write a function to split the given string at uppercase letters by using regex.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to split the given string at uppercase letters by using regex.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: SplitList
Main goal: To parse a string into a list of segments, each starting with an uppercase letter, by using the regex [A-Z][^A-Z]* and collecting all matches into a List<String>.
Notes: It uses a helper method I(int) to convert 0/1 to boolean; contains some no-op statements and unreachable code, but functionally it returns the matching substrings.

mbpp_0027.reference_description: Write a java function to remove all digits from array of strings.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to remove all digits from array of strings.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Digit-stripping transformer: takes a List<String> and returns a new List<String> with all digits removed from each string (via replaceAll("\\d", "")); input is not modified.

mbpp_0043.reference_description: Write a function to find sequences of lowercase letters joined with an underscore using regex.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find sequences of lowercase letters joined with an underscore using regex.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: TextMatcher
Main goal: Check if an input string matches the regex "^[a-z]+_[a-z]+$" (lowercase words separated by an underscore) and return "Found a match!" if it does, otherwise "Not matched!". It uses a helper to convert the regex result to a boolean.

mbpp_0021.reference_description: Write a function to find m number of multiples of n.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find m number of multiples of n.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Computes and returns the first n multiples of n2 as a List<Integer> (n2, 2*n2, ..., n*n2). It iterates from 1 up to n using a helper bound check and multiplies each by n2 to populate the list; if n <= 0 it returns an empty list. Some decompiler artifacts appear but do not affect behavior.

mbpp_0049.reference_description: Write a function to extract every first or specified element from a given two-dimensional array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to extract every first or specified element from a given two-dimensional array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Extract nth element from each sublist
Main goal: Given a List<List<T>> and an index n, return a List<T> containing the nth element from each inner list by iterating the outer list and collecting list.get(n) from each inner list (with some obfuscated/no-op statements in the loop).

mbpp_0154.reference_description: Write a function to extract every specified element from a given two dimensional array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to extract every specified element from a given two dimensional array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: SpecifiedElementExtractor — Extract nth element from each inner list.
Main goal: Given a List<List<T>> and an index n, return a new List<T> containing the element at index n from every inner list.

mbpp_0203.reference_description: Write a java function to find the hamming distance between given two integers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the hamming distance between given two integers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Hamming distance calculator for two integers
Main goal: Compute how many bits differ between two integers by XOR-ing them and counting the number of set bits in the result.
What it does: hammingDistance(n, n2) computes n ^ n2 into n3, then iterates while n3 > 0, accumulating the least-significant bit (n3 & 1) into a counter and shifting n3 right. A helper I(int n) simply checks n > 0. There are some decompiler artifacts (no-op lines) that do not affect the outcome.
Note: The approach is flawed for negative XOR results because it uses a positive-only loop condition with a signed right shift; a correct implementation would loop while n3 != 0 and use unsigned shifts.

mbpp_0145.reference_description: Write a java function to find the maximum difference between any two elements in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the maximum difference between any two elements in a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MaxAbsDiff - Range of first n elements
Main goal: Compute the difference between the maximum and minimum values among the first n elements of the input array (i.e., the range). It scans nArray[0..n-1], tracks the min and max, and returns max - min.

mbpp_0156.reference_description: Write a function to convert a tuple of string values to a tuple of integer values.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to convert a tuple of string values to a tuple of integer values.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: TupleConverter - convert string pairs to integer pairs

Main goal: Provide a utility method that takes a list of 2-element String arrays and returns a List<int[]> where each int[] contains the first two entries parsed as integers. A tiny helper I(n) simply checks n != 0 to drive the loop; some decompiled no-op lines are present but do not affect functionality.

mbpp_0345.reference_description: Write a function to find the difference between two consecutive numbers in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the difference between two consecutive numbers in a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Response: Title: DiffConsecutiveNums - Consecutive Differences Calculator; Main goal: Given a list of integers, return a new list containing the differences between each pair of consecutive elements (list[i+1] - list[i]), by iterating until the second-to-last element (i < size-1); includes some no-op artifacts from decompilation.

mbpp_0205.reference_description: Write a function to find the inversions of tuple elements in the given tuple array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the inversions of tuple elements in the given tuple array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Inversion.inversionElements
Main goal: Return a list where each element is the bitwise complement (~) of the corresponding input integer by iterating through the given list; the extra no-op lines are decompiler artifacts and do not affect the core logic.

mbpp_0236.reference_description: Write a java function to count the maximum number of equilateral triangles that can be formed within a given equilateral triangle.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count the maximum number of equilateral triangles that can be formed within a given equilateral triangle.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
TriangleCounter: a small utility to count triangles in a grid-like arrangement using two inputs.

Main goal: Given n and n2, validate that n >= n2 (return -1 if not) and compute the result as T(n - n2 + 1) + T(n - 2n2 + 1), where T(x) = x*(x+1)/2.

mbpp_0206.reference_description: Write a function to perform the adjacent element concatenation in the given tuples.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to perform the adjacent element concatenation in the given tuples.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Concatenator
Main goal: Given a List<String>, create a new List<String> where each element is the concatenation of two adjacent elements from the input (for i from 0 to size-2, produce list[i] + list[i+1]); returns an empty list if the input has fewer than 2 elements. A helper I(n, n2) checks n < n2. The extra length() calls are no-ops from decompilation and do not affect behavior.

mbpp_0424.reference_description: Write a function to extract only the rear index element of each string in the given tuple.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to extract only the rear index element of each string in the given tuple.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Main goal: Convert a list of strings into a list of their last characters.

What it does: The extractRear method iterates over the input List<String>, and for each non-empty string, it takes the last character (string.charAt(string.length() - 1)) and adds it to a result List<Character>, which is returned at the end. It uses an Iterator and a helper I(int n) that returns true if n != 0 to drive the loop.

Notes: The code contains several decompiler-generated no-op lines (such as empty string length computations and a redundant always-true condition with a continue) that have no effect on behavior. The private I(int n) simply returns whether n is nonzero. Also, empty strings would cause an exception when accessing the last character.

mbpp_0372.reference_description: Write a function to sort a given array of elements in ascending order using heap queue algorithm.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to sort a given array of elements in ascending order using heap queue algorithm.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: HeapSort - ascending sort using PriorityQueue. Main goal: given a List of Comparable elements, build a min-heap (PriorityQueue) from them and poll elements to produce and return a new list in ascending order (a heap-sort-like approach using a priority queue). The code includes decompiled/no-op artifacts but functionally sorts the input by extracting the smallest element repeatedly.

mbpp_0419.reference_description: Write a function to round every number of a given array of numbers and print the total sum multiplied by the length of the array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to round every number of a given array of numbers and print the total sum multiplied by the length of the array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Obfuscated round-and-multiply aggregator for a list of doubles
Main goal: Given a List<Double>, compute the sum of Math.round(d) for all elements, then multiply that sum by the list size, returning the result as a long. The code iterates with an iterator and includes no-op statements introduced by decompilation.

mbpp_0368.reference_description: Write a function to repeat the given tuple n times.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to repeat the given tuple n times.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: TupleRepeater.repeatTuples

Main goal: Return a list containing n references to the supplied list (i.e., n copies of the same List<T>), or an empty list if n <= 0. It does this by iterating n times and adding the same input list to the result each time.

mbpp_0503.reference_description: Write a function to add consecutive numbers of a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to add consecutive numbers of a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Utils.addConsecutiveNums - consecutive pair sum generator
Main goal: Given a list of integers, return a new list where each element is the sum of two adjacent elements from the input list (for i from 0 to size-2, compute list[i] + list[i+1]). If the input has fewer than 2 elements, return an empty list. Includes a tiny helper I(n, n2) that checks n < n2; contains decompiler artifacts.

mbpp_0456.reference_description: Write a function to reverse strings in a given array of string values.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to reverse strings in a given array of string values.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Reverse strings in a list
Main goal: Given a List<String>, return a new List<String> where each string from the input is reversed character-by-character. The original list remains unchanged. The method iterates over the input, reverses each element using StringBuilder(...).reverse(), and adds it to the result. Some obfuscated, no-op code is present but does not affect the outcome.

mbpp_0460.reference_description: Write a java function to get the first element of each sublist.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to get the first element of each sublist.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Goal: Extractor.extract converts a List<List<T>> into a List<T> by taking the first element of each inner list (i.e., collecting sublist.get(0) from every inner list). It iterates the outer list and builds a new list of those first elements, assuming each inner list is non-empty.

mbpp_0433.reference_description: Write a function to check whether the entered number is greater than the elements of the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check whether the entered number is greater than the elements of the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Checks whether a given integer n is strictly greater than all elements in the provided int[] by sorting the array (in place) and comparing n to the array's maximum. Returns a Yes/No message accordingly; equality yields the "No" path and the array is mutated by sorting.

mbpp_0529.reference_description: Write a function to find the nth jacobsthal-lucas number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the nth jacobsthal-lucas number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Jacobsthal-Lucas sequence calculator
Main goal: Compute the nth Jacobsthal-Lucas number using an iterative dynamic-programming approach with base values J(0)=2 and J(1)=1, via the recurrence J(n)=J(n-1)+2*J(n-2), and return J(n).

mbpp_0543.reference_description: Write a function to add two numbers and print number of digits of sum.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to add two numbers and print number of digits of sum.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: CountDigits
Main goal: Compute how many decimal digits are in the sum of two integers (n + n2) when the sum is positive; if the sum is zero or negative, it returns 0. The extra string operations are decompilation artifacts and do not affect the logic.

mbpp_0536.reference_description: Write a function to select the nth items of array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to select the nth items of array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: nthItems utility to sample a list
Main goal: Return a new List containing every nth element from the input list, starting at index 0 (i.e., elements at indices 0, n, 2n, ...). It uses a generic type T and a helper I for bounds checking. Note: Decompiled artifacts like empty statements are present, and the function can infinite-loop or fail if n <= 0.

mbpp_0547.reference_description: Write a java function to find the sum of hamming distances of all consecutive numbers from o to n.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the sum of hamming distances of all consecutive numbers from o to n.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Obfuscated computation of a sum of floor divisions by powers of two.
Main goal: totalHammingDistance(n) computes sum_{k>=0} floor(n / 2^k) for all k where 2^k <= n by iterating powers of two (1, 2, 4, ...) and accumulating n / n2 into a total. A helper I(int n) checks n > 0. There are deliberate no-op lines that don’t affect the outcome, so the function effectively returns the described sum.

mbpp_0565.reference_description: Write a java function to split a string into characters.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to split a string into characters.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: StringUtils.split — Character-wise split into a list
Main goal: Return a List<String> where each element is a single-character string corresponding to the characters of the input string (i.e., split the string into its individual characters).

mbpp_0551.reference_description: Write a function to extract a specified column from a given nested array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to extract a specified column from a given nested array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code defines a generic Extractor with a method extractColumn that, given a List of Lists and an index n, iterates over each inner list, removes the element at position n from that inner list, and collects all removed elements into a new List<T> which it returns. In effect, it extracts a column from a 2D list (while mutating the input rows). The odd no-op statements are artifacts from decompilation/obfuscation.

mbpp_0690.reference_description: Write a function to multiply consecutive numbers of a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to multiply consecutive numbers of a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Goal: Given a list of integers, compute and return a new list containing the products of each pair of consecutive elements (i.e., for i from 0 to size-2, append list[i] * list[i+1]). The private helper I(n, n2) simply checks n < n2 and is used to control the loop. The extra no-op statements (e.g., "".length(); and if (null == null) continue;) are decompiler artifacts and do not affect the outcome.

mbpp_0724.reference_description: Write a function to calculate the sum of all digits of the base to the specified power.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to calculate the sum of all digits of the base to the specified power.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Digit-sum of a power

Main goal: Given two integers n and n2, compute the sum of the decimal digits of n raised to the n2-th power (i.e., the digit sum of n^n2). The code uses BigInteger to calculate n^n2, converts the result to a string, iterates over each digit, converts it to its numeric value, and accumulates the total digits sum. A small helper I(n, n2) simply checks n < n2 for the loop condition. Some decompiled, no-op statements are present but do not affect the overall behavior.

mbpp_0774.reference_description: Write a function to check if the string is a valid email address or not using regex.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if the string is a valid email address or not using regex.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: EmailValidator - regex-based email checker
Main goal: Validate an input string against a regex to determine if it is a valid email and return either "Valid Email" or "Invalid Email". The code defines an unused REGEX constant and a helper I(int) that converts 0/1 to boolean; checkEmail uses Pattern.matches with a literal regex and the I method to decide the result.

mbpp_0763.reference_description: Write a java function to find the minimum difference between any two elements in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the minimum difference between any two elements in a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MinDiffFinder.findMinDiff – Minimum adjacent difference after sorting
Main goal: Sort the input integer array and return the smallest difference between any two consecutive elements. It iterates through adjacent pairs to update the minimum gap and returns that value (note: for arrays with fewer than two elements it returns Integer.MAX_VALUE). The extra seemingly obfuscated lines are no-ops from decompilation and do not affect the outcome.

mbpp_0728.reference_description: Write a function to sum elements in two arrays.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to sum elements in two arrays.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
<Summary_description>
Title: Element-wise summation of two Integer lists (with decompiler artifacts)

Main goal: Create a new list where each element is the sum of the corresponding elements from two input lists.

What it does: sumList(list, list2) builds a new ArrayList<Integer>, iterates with an index n from 0 up to list.size(), and adds list.get(n) + list2.get(n) to the result. It uses helper I(n, n2) to check bounds (n < n2). However, due to inserted no-op statements and an unconditional return null inside the loop, the method actually returns null after the first iteration when the inputs are non-empty (and returns an empty list if inputs are empty).

mbpp_0825.reference_description: Write a java function to access multiple elements of specified index from a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to access multiple elements of specified index from a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Defines a generic Utils class with accessElements(List<T>, List<Integer>) that builds and returns a new list containing elements from the first list at the positions specified by the second list of indices. It iterates over the index list and adds list.get(index) to the result. A small helper I(int) and some decompiler artifacts are present but do not change the core behavior.

mbpp_0902.reference_description: Write a function to combine two maps by adding values for common keys.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to combine two maps by adding values for common keys.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: DictUtils.addDict — Merge and sum integer counts from two maps
Main goal: Return a new map that combines two input maps by summing values for overlapping keys. It copies the first map, iterates over the second map, and for each key adds the second map’s value to the existing value (or uses 0 if the key is new). The input maps remain unmodified. The code appears obfuscated/decompiled and contains no-op statements, but effectively performs a dictionary merge with summing counts.

mbpp_0076.reference_description: Write a java function to count the number of squares in a rectangle.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count the number of squares in a rectangle.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: RectangleSquares - Count total squares in a rectangle grid
Main goal: Given two side lengths l and l2, compute the total number of axis-aligned squares inside an l-by-l2 grid. The code first ensures l ≤ l2 by swapping when needed, then uses a closed-form formula: min*(min+1)*(2*min+1)/6 + (max−min)*min*(min+1)/2, where min = l and max = l2. Helper methods implement the comparison and swap logic.

mbpp_0116.reference_description: Write a function to convert a given tuple of positive integers into an integer.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to convert a given tuple of positive integers into an integer.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: TupleToIntUtil - Concatenate integers into a BigInteger
Main goal: Convert an array of integers into a single BigInteger by concatenating the decimal representations of the elements in order and parsing the result as a BigInteger.

mbpp_0098.reference_description: Write a function to multiply all the numbers in array and divide with the length of the array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to multiply all the numbers in array and divide with the length of the array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Goal: compute (product of all elements in a List<Double>) divided by the number of elements. The method multiplies all numbers in a loop and returns product / n; for an empty list it yields Infinity. There are intentional no-ops and obfuscated checks (e.g., the I method and strange constant expressions) that do not affect the outcome; the overall effect is just a product-then-divide operation.

mbpp_0261.reference_description: Write a function to perform mathematical division operation across the given tuples.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to perform mathematical division operation across the given tuples.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Element-wise division of two integer arrays
Main goal: The code computes a new array whose elements are the quotients of corresponding elements from two input int arrays, up to the length of the shorter array, effectively performing pairwise division until the shorter input ends. It uses a small helper to check the loop bound. Note: The decompiled snippet includes some dead/unreachable code and does not handle division-by-zero.

mbpp_0197.reference_description: Write a function to perform the exponentiation of the given two tuples.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to perform the exponentiation of the given two tuples.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The Exponentiation class provides a static method findExponentio that takes two double arrays and returns a new array whose i-th element is dArray[i] raised to the power dArray2[i], for i from 0 up to the minimum length of the two input arrays. It performs element-wise exponentiation using Math.pow and uses a helper I to test the loop bound. The code as shown contains decompiler remnants (nonsense lines like "".length(); and if (null == null) continue; return null;) that are not functional in a normal build, indicating artifacts from decompilation rather than intentional logic. The goal is element-wise exponentiation of two arrays with length safety via the min-length.

mbpp_0213.reference_description: Write a function to perform the concatenation of two string tuples.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to perform the concatenation of two string tuples.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: StringConcatenator - Concatenate corresponding elements of two string arrays
Main goal: Given two string arrays, produce a new array where each element is the concatenation of the corresponding elements from the inputs, computed up to the length of the shorter array. If one array is longer, its extra elements are ignored. The operation is driven by a helper method that checks the loop condition.

mbpp_0224.reference_description: Write a java function to count set bits of a given number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count set bits of a given number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: BitCounter
Main goal: Implement a function to count the number of set bits (1s) in a 32-bit integer. countSetBits(int n) iterates while n is nonzero, accumulating the least-significant bit (n & 1) into a counter and shifting n right by one each loop, using a helper I(int n) to test non-zeroness. The code contains decompiler artifacts (no-op strings and checks) that don’t affect the outcome.

mbpp_0347.reference_description: Write a java function to count the number of squares in a rectangle.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count the number of squares in a rectangle.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Count squares in a grid
Main goal: Compute the total number of axis-aligned squares in an m×n grid. It first swaps the inputs so the first dimension is the larger side, then returns min(m,n) * (min(m,n) + 1) * (3*max(m,n) − min(m,n) + 1) / 6 as a long.

mbpp_0399.reference_description: Write a function to perform the mathematical bitwise xor operation across the given tuples.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to perform the mathematical bitwise xor operation across the given tuples.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Bitwise XOR of two int arrays (element-wise up to the shorter length)

Main goal: Return a new int[] where each element i is the bitwise XOR of nArray[i] and nArray2[i], computed for i from 0 to min(nArray.length, nArray2.length) - 1; any extra elements beyond the shorter input are ignored. The code includes a small helper for the loop condition and some decompiler artifacts that do not affect functionality.

mbpp_0271.reference_description: Write a java function to find the sum of fifth power of first n even natural numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the sum of fifth power of first n even natural numbers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: EvenPowerSum
Main goal: Compute the sum of the fifth powers of the first n even integers, i.e., sum_{i=1}^n (2i)^5, using a simple loop to accumulate the result.

mbpp_0365.reference_description: Write a java function to count the number of digits of a given number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count the number of digits of a given number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: DigitCounter - Digit counting utility
Main goal: Determine how many decimal digits are in a given integer (returning 0 for input 0). It does this by repeatedly dividing the number by 10 and counting iterations until the value becomes 0.
Functions:
- countDigit(int n): starts with count 0, then while n != 0, divides n by 10 and increments the counter. Contains decompiler-inserted no-op lines that do not affect behavior.
- I(int n): helper that returns true if n != 0; used as the loop condition.
Notes: For positive n, returns the number of digits. For n = 0, returns 0. For negative n, behavior follows integer division toward zero and may yield 1 in some cases.

mbpp_0420.reference_description: Write a java function to find the cube sum of first n even natural numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the cube sum of first n even natural numbers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: CubeSum - Sum of even cubes up to n
Main goal: The cubeSum(n) method computes the sum of cubes of even numbers from 2 up to 2n by iterating k from 1 to n and adding (2k)^3. This yields 2 * n^2 * (n + 1)^2 for n >= 1 (and 0 if n <= 0). The helper I(int n, int m) simply checks whether n <= m.

mbpp_0429.reference_description: Write a function to extract the elementwise and tuples from the given two tuples.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to extract the elementwise and tuples from the given two tuples.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: andTuples — element-wise bitwise AND of two int arrays
Main goal: Given two int arrays, produce a new array whose length is the smaller of the two inputs, where each element at index i is the result of nArray[i] & nArray2[i]. Extra elements from the longer array are ignored. A tiny helper method I(a, b) simply checks a < b to drive the loop.

mbpp_0439.reference_description: Write a function to convert array of multiple integers into a single integer.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to convert array of multiple integers into a single integer.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Converter.multipleToSingle
Main goal: Take a List<Integer>, append each element to a StringBuilder to form a decimal string, then parse that string as an int, effectively concatenating the elements into a single number. It uses a convoluted helper to drive the loop and lacks handling for an empty list (would throw).

mbpp_0422.reference_description: Write a java function to find the average of cubes of first n natural numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the average of cubes of first n natural numbers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Average of cubes from 1 to n
Main goal: Compute the average of the cubes of integers from 1 to n (i.e., (1^3 + 2^3 + ... + n^3) / n) and round the result to six decimal places. It iterates from 1 to n, sums n2^3, divides by n, and returns the rounded value. The odd strings/length checks are decompiler artifacts that have no effect on the outcome.

mbpp_0494.reference_description: Write a function to convert the given binary tuple to integer.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to convert the given binary tuple to integer.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code defines a method binaryToInteger that takes an array of integers (expected to be binary digits 0 or 1), concatenates them into a binary string, parses that string as a base-2 integer, and returns its decimal representation as a String. A helper method I(n, n2) simply checks n < n2 and is used as the loop condition. Some decompiled no-op statements are present but do not affect the logic.

mbpp_0500.reference_description: Write a function to concatenate all elements of the given array into a string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to concatenate all elements of the given array into a string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Concatenator - Joins a list of strings with spaces
Main goal: Take a List<String> and produce a single string by iterating the list and appending a space followed by each element. The result begins with an extra leading space (and effectively uses double spaces before the first element). If the list is empty, it returns a single space. The code uses a helper method I to drive the loop and contains some dead/no-op statements inside the loop.

mbpp_0449.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the triangle is valid or not if 3 points are given.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the triangle is valid or not if 3 points are given.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: TriangleValidityChecker

Main goal: Given six integers representing three 2D points (x1,y1), (x2,y2), (x3,y3), compute twice the signed area of the triangle using the shoelace determinant. If the area is zero, the points are collinear (not a triangle) and the method returns "No"; otherwise it returns "Yes". The helper I(int n) simply checks for zero area.

mbpp_0470.reference_description: Write a function to find the pairwise addition of the elements of the given tuples.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the pairwise addition of the elements of the given tuples.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Pairwise Adjacent Sum Calculator
Main goal: The code defines a method addPairwise that, given an int array, returns a new array of length n-1 where each element is the sum of two consecutive elements of the input (i.e., [a0+a1, a1+a2, ..., a_{n-2}+a_{n-1}]). It iterates with a helper I(n, m) that checks n < m to control the loop, fills the result array, and returns it. There are some extraneous lines (from decompilation) like "" .length(); and if (null == null) continue; return null; which do not affect the actual logic. Note: if the input array is empty (length 0), the code would attempt to allocate a negative-length array (length -1) and fail; otherwise it works for length >= 1.

mbpp_0549.reference_description: Write a java function to find the sum of fifth power of first n odd natural numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the sum of fifth power of first n odd natural numbers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Sum of fifth powers of the first n odd numbers

Main goal: The code computes and returns the sum S(n) = 1^5 + 3^5 + 5^5 + ... + (2n−1)^5 as a long. It iterates n2 from 1 to n, computes the current odd number l2 = 2·n2−1, raises it to the 5th power, accumulates it in l, and returns l. A helper I(n, n2) simply checks n ≤ n2 to bound the loop. The odd-looking strings/length() calls are meaningless decompiler artifacts and do not affect the computation.

mbpp_0616.reference_description: Write a function to perfom the modulo of tuple elements in the given two tuples.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to perfom the modulo of tuple elements in the given two tuples.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: TupleModulo

Main goal: Compute an element-wise modulo of two int arrays up to the length of the shorter array, returning a new array with the modulo results (a[i] % b[i]).

Summary of functionality:
- The method tupleModulo(int[] nArray, int[] nArray2) creates a result array whose length is the minimum of the two input arrays.
- It fills result[i] with nArray[i] % nArray2[i] for i from 0 to minLength-1.
- It uses a small helper I(int n, int n2) to check the loop bound (n < n2).
- There is intentionally obfuscated/dead code (e.g., "" .length(); if (null == null) continue; return null;) that does not affect the actual computation.
- Edge cases: if an element of nArray2 is zero, a ArithmeticException may be thrown; if either input is empty, the result is an empty array.

mbpp_0558.reference_description: Write a java function to find the digit distance between two integers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the digit distance between two integers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: DigitDistance
Main goal: Return the sum of the decimal digits of the absolute difference between two integers (i.e., sum of digits of |n - n2|). It computes |n - n2|, converts the result to a string, and sums each digit's numeric value.

mbpp_0634.reference_description: Write a java function to find the sum of fourth power of first n even natural numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the sum of fourth power of first n even natural numbers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: EvenPowerSum
Goal: Compute the sum of the fourth powers of even numbers from 2 up to 2n (i.e., sum_{i=1}^n (2i)^4) using an iterative loop and return it as a long.

mbpp_0686.reference_description: Write a function to find the frequency of each element in the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the frequency of each element in the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
FrequencyCounter: Element frequency counter for a list
Main goal: Compute how many times each element occurs in a given List<T> and return a string representation of the resulting frequency map.

Notes:
- The code builds a HashMap<T, Integer> to count occurrences via getOrDefault and increments for each element.
- It uses an obfuscated loop with a helper I(int n) to drive the while condition, but effectively it iterates until the list is exhausted.
- It returns the hash map’s string form (e.g., {a=2, b=1}) and contains some dead/odd lines from decompilation (unreachable return and redundant string length checks).

mbpp_0677.reference_description: Write a function to check if the triangle is valid or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if the triangle is valid or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: TriangleValidator - checks if three angles form a valid triangle
Main goal: Determine whether the sum of three integer angles equals 180 degrees. validityTriangle(n, n2, n3) adds the three values and returns true if their sum is 180; it uses a private helper to compare integers for equality.

mbpp_0673.reference_description: Write a java function to convert array of multiple integers into a single integer.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to convert array of multiple integers into a single integer.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Goal: Take a List<Integer>, iterate through it, concatenate the decimal representations of all elements into one string, then parse that string as an int and return it (e.g., [12, 3] -> 123). It uses a StringBuilder and an iterator, then converts the result to an int. Note: there is dead/unreachable code inside the loop (an always-true condition with a continue) likely from decompiled/obfuscated source.

mbpp_0715.reference_description: Write a function to convert the given string of integers into a tuple.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to convert the given string of integers into a tuple.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Converter.strToTuple converts a comma-space separated string to an int array
Main goal: Parse a string formatted as "n1, n2, ..., nk" into an int[] by splitting on ", " and converting each token to an integer; uses a simple bound-check helper for the loop.

mbpp_0761.reference_description: Write a function to caluclate arc length of an angle.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to caluclate arc length of an angle.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: ArcLengthCalculator

Main goal: Compute the arc length of a circular arc from a given diameter and central angle in degrees using an approximate pi (3.142857...). It returns null if the angle is 360 degrees or more. The formula used is s = (π * diameter * angle) / 360. The class includes two tiny helper methods for basic comparison logic.

mbpp_0770.reference_description: Write a java function to find the sum of fourth power of first n odd natural numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the sum of fourth power of first n odd natural numbers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: OddNumSum – Sum of fourth powers of the first n odd numbers

Main goal: Compute the sum of the fourth powers of the first n odd integers, i.e., sum_{k=1}^n (2k−1)^4, and return it as a long.
